61.s: Which of the following pairs correctly states the number of subjects in the Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules, respectively?
61.x: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects relating to Panchayats, while the Twelfth Schedule contains 18 subjects relating to municipalities.
61.tq: Keep the Panchayat and municipal Schedule counts in their constitutional order.
xs: The **Eleventh Schedule** has **29** subjects (panchayats) and the **Twelfth Schedule** **18** (municipalities) — option **(2)**: 29 and 18.
Option (1) reverses them — the classic trap.
xa: **Neither Schedule transfers anything by itself**; Art. **243G/243W** say the State "**may**" devolve.
Panchayat taxing powers: **243H**; municipal equivalent: **243X**.
The 3Fs: **Functions**, **Funds**, **Functionaries**.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about local devolution in practice:
1. In practice, 3F devolution typically means functions are devolved on paper, funds arrive tied to schemes, and staff report to State line departments.
2. The District Planning Committee and the Metropolitan Planning Committee are provided under Article 243ZD and Article 243ZE respectively.
3. Andhra Pradesh reserves one-third of the seats in Panchayats for women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x:
Statement 1: Correct: functions exist on paper, funds are commonly tied to schemes, and functionaries report to State line departments.
Statement 2: Correct: the DPC is under Article 243ZD and the MPC under Article 243ZE.
Statement 3: Incorrect: one-third is only the constitutional minimum under Article 243D; Andhra Pradesh reserves 50 per cent.

61.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a reason for the underperformance of Panchayati Raj Institutions in the government's Roadmap for Panchayati Raj?
o: Weak devolution of the three Fs
61.x: The Roadmap identifies weak 3F devolution, bureaucratic control, tied funds, dependence on grants and reluctance to tax. Complete financial autonomy is not listed and contradicts the identified constraints.
61.tq: Find the option that reverses the diagnosed weakness instead of merely naming one.
xs: **Complete financial autonomy** is NOT a reason — panchayats actually **depend on grants** — option **(1)**.
The **Roadmap** lists: **weak 3F devolution**, **bureaucratic control**, **tied funds**, **dependence on grants**, **reluctance to tax**.
xa: ULB own revenue is only **~0.3% of GDP**.
Funds **arrive tied** to schemes; staff report to **State line departments**.

61.s: Which constitutional arrangement ended the practice of postponing local elections at will?
o: Appointment of Special Officers for every local body
Elections held at the discretion of the State Government
A three-year term renewable by the State Government
A five-year term, with elections before expiry or within six months of dissolution, under the SEC
61.x: The five-year term with elections before expiry or within six months of dissolution, conducted by the State Election Commission, made local government a permanent institution after 1993.
xa: Term: **243E** (panchayats) / **243U** (municipalities); SEC: **243K** / **243ZA**.
**Special Officers** run AP local bodies whose terms lapsed.
16th FC grants go only to **properly constituted** local bodies.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about local body finances:
1. The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules do not transfer subjects to local bodies automatically without legislative action.
2. Property tax is the single most important source of own revenue for Urban Local Bodies.
3. Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants for 2026–31, the urban share increased from 36% to 45%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Schedules do not transfer subjects automatically; Articles 243G and 243W use the discretionary 'may'.
Statement 2: Correct: property tax is the main own-source revenue of ULBs, though under-assessed and under-collected.
Statement 3: Correct: the urban share rises to 45%, with grants split 80% basic and 20% performance.

61.s:
With reference to the finances of Urban Local Bodies, consider the following statements:
1. Their own-source revenue is only about 0.3% of GDP.
2. Cities produce about 67% of GDP.
3. Cities receive more than half of the country’s tax revenue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because cities receive less than 1% of tax revenue, despite producing about two-thirds of GDP.
61.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the revenue-share statement.
xs: Statement 1 correct: ULB own revenue is only **~0.3% of GDP**.
Statement 2 correct: cities produce **~2/3 (about 67%) of GDP**.
Statement 3 wrong: cities get **<1%** of tax revenue. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: **GST** cost ULBs ~**19%** of own revenue (octroi, entry tax).
ULBs **depend on tied grants**; property registers outdated.
**Weak balance sheets** keep most bodies out of the bond market.

61.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: State Election Commissioner – Removed like a High Court Judge
Chief Election Commissioner – Removed like a High Court Judge
State Election Commissioner – Appointed by the President
Elections to Municipalities – Conducted by the Election Commission of India
61.x: Under Article 243K the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and removable only like a High Court Judge; the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court Judge.
xa: **243K** for panchayats; **243ZA** for municipalities.
SEC + **5-year term** + **6-month rule** made local government **permanent**.
**Before 1993**, States postponed local polls at will.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about local bodies and Andhra Pradesh:
1. In debates on local devolution, Janmabhoomi committees and secretariats are criticised as bodies elected under the 73rd Amendment.
2. The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet decision of 18 August 2026 provided 34% reservation for Backward Classes in rural local bodies.
3. The Backward Regions Grant Fund was merged into the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: they are criticised as parallel bodies that weaken the centrality of PRIs.
Statement 2: Correct: it provided 34% BC reservation in rural local bodies and 33⅓% in urban local bodies.
Statement 3: Correct: the BRGF was merged into RGSA (APPSC-GS 2018).

61.s: Which of the following is identified as an arrangement that bypasses elected local bodies?
61.x: DRDAs, user groups, SHGs and MPLADS/MLA LADS bypass elected local bodies; DPCs and MPCs are constitutional planning bodies.
xa: Under **MPLADS/MLA LADS**, **legislators pick the works**.
**Parastatals** and **SPVs** also bypass elected bodies and citizen participation.
The proposed **District Development Council** was criticised as a **parallel executive**.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about local governance and its support:
1. Village and ward secretariats and volunteers were introduced in Andhra Pradesh in 2019.
2. Properly constituted local bodies are not a condition associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission's local-body grants.
3. Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, begun in 2018-19, strengthens Panchayati Raj Institutions mainly for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x:
Statement 1: Correct: they were introduced in 2019, after the Janmabhoomi committees of 2014-19.
Statement 2: Incorrect: properly constituted local bodies are a condition, with audited accounts and timely State Finance Commissions; permanent Special Officers are not.
Statement 3: Correct: RGSA aims to strengthen PRIs so that they can help achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

61.s:
With reference to MPLADS, consider the following statements:
1. The Member of Parliament recommends works, which the Implementing District Authority executes.
2. RTI applies to works under the scheme.
3. The Member of Parliament executes the works directly.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
61.x: Under MPLADS the MP only recommends works and the Implementing District Authority executes them; RTI applies and eSAKSHI is the associated portal.
xa: MPLADS/MLA LADS are criticised as bypassing PRIs because **legislators pick the works**.
Other parallel bodies: **DRDAs**, user groups, **SHGs**, **parastatals/SPVs**.

61.s:
Assertion (A): Delayed local-body elections can jeopardise the flow of Central grants to local bodies.
Reason (R): The Sixteenth Finance Commission links grants with properly constituted local bodies, audited accounts and timely State Finance Commissions.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
61.x: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the grant conditions explain why failure to constitute elected local bodies and related institutions can put Central funds at risk.
61.tq: Test whether the financial consequence is directly explained by the stated grant conditions.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
R is true: the **16th FC** ties grants to **properly constituted** local bodies, **published audited accounts** and **timely SFCs**.
A follows from R: delayed polls put grants at risk — that is why AP is **rushing polls**, with **₹12,150 crore** at risk if not done by **October**.

The functions of Election Commission of India are-
(I) To conduct all the elections of the Parliament and State Legislative Assembly.
(II) To conduct elections for the post of President and Vice-President.
(III) To recommend for President’s Rule in case of any State not in condition to hold or conduct free and fair elections in any State.
(IV) To Supervise, direct and control the work of preparing electoral lists.
62.x: According to Article 324 (1), the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to Parliament and the Legislature of every State and elections to the offices of President and Vice-President held under this Constitution shall be vested in an Election Commission. Note- The Election Commission does not recommend the President’s Rule in case any State is not in a condition to conduct free and fair elections.

62.s: In which part of the Indian Constitution, have the provisions for elections been made ?
62.x: Part XV of the Constitution (Articles 324 to 329) is titled “Elections”. It contains the constitutional framework for the establishment and powers of the Election Commission, preparation of electoral rolls, and conduct of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and for the offices of the President and Vice-President.

62.s: The status of the Chief Election Commissioner of India is equal to the –
o: Speaker of Legislative Assembly of a State
62.x: Article 324 of the Constitution provides superintendence, direction, and control of the Parliament and State Legislature elections to be vested in an Election Commission. Thus assertion (A) is correct. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from his post in like manner and on the like grounds as provided for the removal of Judges from the Supreme Court. The other members can be removed by the President in consultation with the Chief Election Commissioner. Thus, reason (R) is also correct, but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

62.s: For election to the Panchayat, the State Election Commissioner will be appointed by
o: The Chief Election Commissioner of India
62.x: A State Election Commission is constituted under Article 243K to conduct all elections of the Panchayats. The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor of the State.

62.s:
Study the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below:
Assertion (A) : The State Election Commission is a Constitutional authority.
Reason (R) : Elections to rural local bodies are overseen by the Election Commission of India.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
62.x: The State Election Commission is constituted under the 73rd and 74th Constitutional ( Amendments) Acts of 1992, for each State / Union Territory. SECs are vested with the powers of conducting the elections to the corporations, municipalities, Zilla Parishads, District Panchayats, Panchayat Samitis, Gram Panchayats and other local bodies. The Election Commission of India has no role in these elections.

62.s: Under which Article the State Election Commission Operates the election of urban bodies?

Consider the following functions of State Election Commission and select the correct answer using the code given below?
1. Prepares the electoral rolls for Panchayats and Municipalities elections in the State.
2. Conducts elections for Panchayats and Municipalities of the State.
3. Conducts elections for other bodies in addition to Panchayats and Municipalities in accordance with the directions given by the Governor.
4. Prepares the electoral rolls and conducts elections as assigned by Election Commission of India.
62.x: According to Article 243-K(1) and 243-ZA(1), the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to the Panchayats and Municipalities shall be vested in the State Election Commission.

62.s: All elections to the Panchayats are conducted by-
62.x: The Constitution of India vests in the State Election Commission, consisting of a State Election Commissioner, the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of all elections to the Panchayats (Article-243 K) and the Municipalities (Article 243 ZA). The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor. The detailed provisions of the State Election Commission are under the Article 243K itself.

62.s: Which of the following elections is not conducted by the Election Commission?
62.x: Article 324 of the Constitution provides superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, the Parliament and every State Legislature President and Vice-President elections to be vested in an Election Commission. Under Articles 243 K and 243 ZA, the elections of Panchayats and municipalities are conducted by State Election Commission.

62.s: Who conducts the State Assembly Elections?
62.x: According to Article 324, the Election Commission of India conducts the elections of State Assemblies.

62.s: The decision to conduct Panchayat Elections is taken by which of the following?
62.x: Panchayat is enumerated in State List as the 5th entry in the 7th Schedule to the Constitution. It is the subject of State Government, and the State Government has the power to constitute it and conduct its elections through the State Election Commission.

62.s:
Consider the following statements regarding State Election Commission, Rajasthan -
1. The State Election Commission, Rajasthan was constituted in December, 1994
2. It has a secretary who is also the Chief Electoral Officer for the state.
62.x: The State Election Commission, Rajasthan, was constituted in July, 1994. It is a one-member body institute, which has a secretary who is also the chief Electoral officer for the state.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about electoral systems and rolls:
1. Under first-past-the-post in Lok Sabha elections, a candidate wins by securing at least two-thirds of the valid votes.
2. A Special Intensive Revision rebuilds the electoral roll comprehensively.
3. The State Legislative Assembly is elected from single-member territorial constituencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: FPTP needs only the most votes (a plurality) in a single-member constituency.
Statement 2: Correct: a Special Intensive Revision rebuilds the roll, whereas summary revision is conducted annually.
Statement 3: Correct: Assembly members are directly elected from single-member territorial constituencies by first-past-the-post.

63.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as a reason for rejecting proportional representation for Lok Sabha elections?
o: It may encourage fragmentation and unstable governments.
It guarantees a direct election in every single-member constituency.
It weakens the voter–Member of Parliament link.
It may be difficult for voters to understand.
63.x: Difficulty for voters, fragmentation, unstable governments, expense, absence of by-elections and a weaker voter–MP link are cited concerns. Guaranteeing direct election in every single-member constituency is not such a reason.
63.tq: Find the option that is outside the stated list of objections to proportional representation.
xs: "It **guarantees a direct election in every single-member constituency**" is not a cited reason — option **(2)**; single-member constituencies are a feature of **FPTP**.
Cited reasons: **hard for voters**, **fragmentation and unstable** governments, **weakens voter-MP link** — options (1), (3), (4).
xa: Other reasons: PR is **expensive** and allows **no by-elections**.
PR (STV) is used for **Rajya Sabha, Legislative Councils, President, Vice-President**.
Under FPTP the winner is the one with the **most votes (plurality)**.

63.s: Which of the following statements about NOTA in Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections is incorrect?
o: NOTA continues to be applicable in these elections because they are indirect elections.
NOTA is not applicable in Rajya Sabha elections.
NOTA is not applicable in Legislative Council elections.
The Supreme Court struck down NOTA in these elections in 2018.
63.x: Option A is incorrect: the Supreme Court struck down NOTA for Rajya Sabha and Council elections in 2018. NOTA applies only to direct Lok Sabha and Assembly elections.
63.tq: Recall the 2018 ruling on indirect elections.
n: NOTA is not applicable in Rajya Sabha elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
NOTA is not applicable in Legislative Council elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
The Supreme Court struck down NOTA for Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections in 2018. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
NOTA is limited to direct Lok Sabha elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
NOTA is limited to direct Assembly elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **NOTA continues to apply** in Rajya Sabha and Council elections — option **(1)**.
The **Supreme Court struck down** NOTA for **Rajya Sabha** and **Legislative Council** elections in **2018**.
NOTA is limited to **direct Lok Sabha** and **Assembly** elections.
xa: Rajya Sabha and Councils use **PR-STV** (indirect).
NOTA symbol: ballot with a black cross by **NID, Ahmedabad**.
NOTA first used in the Lok Sabha in **2014**.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about NOTA and indirect elections:
1. NOTA is not applicable in Rajya Sabha elections.
2. The Vice-President of India is elected by all MPs, elected and nominated.
3. The Vice-President is elected under Article 61.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: NOTA does not apply to Rajya Sabha or Legislative Council elections.
Statement 2: Correct: the Vice-President is elected by all MPs, elected and nominated, by single transferable vote.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the Vice-President is elected under Article 66, not Article 61.

63.s:
Assertion (A): State Legislatures have no role in the election of the Vice-President.
Reason (R): The Vice-President is elected by all MPs of both Houses, including nominated MPs.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
63.x: Both are true: the Vice-President is elected only by MPs (elected and nominated), which is why State Legislatures have no role. R explains A.
63.tq: Contrast the Vice-President's electoral college with the President's.
n: State Legislative Assembly members have no role in electing the Vice-President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
State Legislative Council members have no role in electing the Vice-President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Vice-President is elected by all Members of Parliament, both elected and nominated. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
All Members of Parliament form the Vice-Presidential electoral college. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Elected Members of Parliament form part of the Vice-Presidential electoral college. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Nominated Members of Parliament form part of the Vice-Presidential electoral college. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
State Legislatures are completely excluded from the Vice-Presidential electoral college. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
The **Vice-President** is elected by **all Members of Parliament** — **elected** and **nominated** — so State Legislatures have no role.
xa: VP election: **Article 66**; **indirect**, PR-STV, **secret ballot**.
⚠ The **President's** electoral college includes **elected MLAs** (**Article 54**).
President/VP disputes go to the **Supreme Court** (**Article 71**).

63.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
63.x: Article 325 provides for one general electoral roll and prohibits exclusion on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex. Article 324 concerns the Election Commission, Article 326 adult suffrage, and Article 329 court-related bars.
63.tq: Use the Article-subject pairing rather than relying on familiar article numbers.
xs: **Article 325** provides for **one general electoral roll** — so option **(2)** is correctly matched.
Art. 325 also bars exclusion from the roll on grounds of **religion, race, caste or sex**.
**Article 324** = **ECI** superintendence, direction and control; **Article 326** = **adult suffrage**; **Article 329** = **bar on courts** (election petitions).
xa: **Articles 327 / 328**: **Parliament / State legislature** may make election laws.
Elections are dealt with in **Part XV**, **Articles 324-329**.
**Local polls** are run by **State Election Commissions** (**Arts. 243K, 243ZA**), not the ECI.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about voting and representation:
1. Under Article 326, a citizen aged 18 or above may be disqualified from voting on grounds of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt practice.
2. A candidate's security deposit is forfeited when the candidate secures less than one-tenth of the valid votes.
3. The constitutional principle underlying delimitation is "one person, one vote, one value".
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Article 326 grants adult suffrage subject to such disqualifications.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the deposit is forfeited below one-sixth of the valid votes, not one-tenth.
Statement 3: Correct: delimitation rests on 'one person, one vote, one value', linked to uniformity of representation under Article 81(2).

63.s:
Consider the following statements about electoral rolls and voters:
1. 1 December is not one of the qualifying dates for revision of electoral rolls.
2. An overseas Indian elector may enrol in the electoral roll at the address of the Indian passport.
3. The 'Sahulat' app was a Jammu and Kashmir initiative for elderly voters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the four qualifying dates are 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.
Statement 2: Correct: under Section 20A of the RPA, 1950, an overseas elector may enrol at the passport address.
Statement 3: Correct: the Sahulat app was a Jammu and Kashmir initiative for elderly voters (APPSC 2019).

63.s:
Consider the following statements about elections and voting rights:
1. The constitutional authority for conducting State Legislative Assembly elections is the State Election Commission.
2. In the Kuldip Nayar case (2006), the Supreme Court held the right to vote to be a statutory right.
3. Article 83, which may need amending for simultaneous elections, deals with the duration of State Legislatures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Assembly elections are run by the Election Commission of India.
Statement 2: Correct: Kuldip Nayar held the right to vote statutory, not fundamental.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Article 83 concerns the duration of the Houses of Parliament; Articles 172 and 174 concern the States.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about voting rights and rules:
1. The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Amendment Act, 1988.
2. Under the old Rule 49-O, a voter entered the booth but refused to vote before the Presiding Officer.
3. A candidate forfeits the security deposit on securing not more than one-sixth of the valid votes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age to 18.
Statement 2: Correct: old Rule 49-O meant refusing to vote before the presiding officer; NOTA means pressing a button on the EVM.
Statement 3: Correct: a candidate with one-sixth or less of the valid votes forfeits the deposit.

63.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The right to vote is a Fundamental Right.
2. The right to contest an election is a statutory right.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
63.x: The right to vote is statutory, not fundamental; the right to contest is also statutory (Kuldip Nayar, 2006).
n: The right to contest elections is a legal or statutory right. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The right to vote is not a Fundamental Right. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The right to vote is a legal or statutory right. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Supreme Court established the statutory nature of the right to vote and the right to contest in Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India in 2006. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The right to contest elections is not a Fundamental Right. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xa: Basis: **RPA 1950 Section 19** and **RPA 1951**.
**Article 326** gives the vote to every citizen aged **18+** unless disqualified.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about elections and delimitation:
1. Former Rule 49-O was struck down because recording a voter's refusal to vote in Form 17-A compromised secrecy.
2. The 70th Constitutional Amendment Act added Delhi and Puducherry to the Presidential electoral college.
3. The Delimitation Commission is headed by the Union Law Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: recording the refusal in Form 17-A broke the secrecy of the vote.
Statement 2: Correct: the 70th Amendment (1992) added the elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry to the electoral college.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the Delimitation Commission is headed by a retired Supreme Court judge.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about local elections and delimitation:
1. Elections to panchayats and municipalities are conducted by State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
2. Under the Delimitation Act of 1972, the Delimitation Commission was constituted in 1973.
3. The 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001 permitted rationalisation of constituencies on the basis of the 1971 Census.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Panchayat and municipal polls are run by the State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA, not by the ECI.
Statement 2: Correct: the Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the 84th Amendment allowed rationalisation using the 1991 Census, not the 1971 Census.

63.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Delimitation Commissions is NOT correctly matched?
63.x: The 1973 Commission was chaired by Justice J.L. Kapur. Justice Kuldip Singh chaired the 2002 Commission.
63.tq: Find the swapped chairperson in a date-person matching question.
xs: **1973 — Justice Kuldip Singh** is wrong — option **(2)**; the 1973 Commission was chaired by **Justice J.L. Kapur**.
Correct: **2002 — Kuldip Singh**, **1963 — J.L. Kapur**, **1952 — N. Chandrasekhara Aiyar**.
xa: ⚠ **J.L. Kapur** chaired two Commissions (**1963, 1973**).
**J&K** Delimitation Commission: **Justice Ranjana Desai** (orders effective March/May **2022**).
Delimitation orders **cannot be challenged in court**.

63.s: Which one of the following statements about the Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution is NOT correct?
o: It proposed freezing the Lok Sabha at 543 seats permanently.
It proposed retaining a 2.2:1 Lok Sabha to Rajya Sabha ratio.
It linked the proposed women’s quota to delimitation from 2029.
It proposed women’s quota from 2029 without linking it to delimitation.
63.x: The resolution proposed women’s reservation from 2029 without linking it to delimitation. It also proposed a permanent freeze at 543 Lok Sabha seats and retention of the 2.2:1 ratio.
63.tq: Locate the reversal of an expressly stated condition in a policy-resolution question.
xs: The resolution did **not link** the **women's quota** to delimitation — so option **(3)** is NOT correct.
It proposed women's quota **from 2029 without linking it to delimitation**, a **permanent freeze at 543**, and the **2.2:1** Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha ratio.
xa: Resolution dated **17 Aug 2026**; southern States fear losing seats to **UP, Bihar, Rajasthan**.
**131st Amendment Bill, 2026** (ceiling **550 to 850**) was defeated — **298 for, 230 against**.
EAC-PM (2026) suggested splitting **170** oversized seats to reach **824**.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about delimitation of constituencies:
1. The Lok Sabha at present has 543 elected seats, against a constitutional ceiling of 550.
2. Readjustment of State Legislative Assembly constituencies after each census is provided under Article 81(2).
3. The freeze on inter-State allocation of Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 1971 Census was first imposed by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, till 2000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats against a ceiling of 550.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Article 170 provides for readjustment of Assembly constituencies; Article 81(2) embodies uniformity of representation.
Statement 3: Correct: the 42nd Amendment (1976) froze inter-State seat allocation on the 1971 Census till 2000.

63.s: Which of the following pairs (Lok Sabha – year of election) is correctly matched?
63.x: The 1st, 9th, 11th and 16th Lok Sabhas were elected in 1952, 1989, 1996 and 2014 respectively.
xa: ⚠ APPSC **2019** answer was **17** elections (correct then).

63.s:
Consider the following statements about delimitation and party recognition:
1. The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposed raising the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 850.
2. The increase in Andhra Pradesh–Telangana seats under Section 26 awaits only a Constitutional Amendment.
3. Recognition of political parties and reservation of symbols is governed by the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Bill proposed 850 seats with delimitation on the 2011 Census, but it was defeated.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the seat increase under Section 26 awaits the first census after 2026.
Statement 3: Correct: the 1968 Order recognises parties and reserves symbols.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about delimitation:
1. It redraws territorial constituency boundaries on the basis of recent census figures.
2. It is intended to ensure equal representation.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
63.x: Delimitation redraws boundaries using recent census figures so that each seat has roughly equal population.
n: Delimitation is the statutory process of redrawing territorial constituency boundaries. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Delimitation is based on recent census figures. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Delimitation enforces equal representation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
xa: Principle: "**one person, one vote, one value**" (APPSC-G1 2024).
**Floating constituency:** **Sangha (Sikkim)** — only registered Buddhist monks vote and contest.
First general election: **1951-52**.

63.s:
Assertion (A): Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be questioned in court.
Reason (R): Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be modified by legislatures.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
63.x: Both are true: Delimitation Commission orders cannot be challenged in court, and legislatures cannot change them. These are two separate safeguards, so R does not explain A.
63.tq: Ask whether two parallel safeguards explain each other.
n: Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be questioned in court. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be modified by legislatures. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A: **Delimitation Commission** orders **cannot be called in question** in **any court** (**Article 329**).
R: they **cannot be modified** by **Parliament** or **State Assemblies** — a separate safeguard.
xa: Orders have the **force of law**.
**Four** Commissions so far — **1952, 1963, 1973, 2002**.
⚠ **J.L. Kapur** chaired two (**1963, 1973**).

63.s:
Which of the following statements are correct?
I. The RPA, 1950 is connected with Articles 81, 82, 170, 171, 325 and 326.
II. The RPA, 1951 is connected with Articles 84, 102, 173, 191, 324 and 329.
III. Article 329 is listed as a constitutional connection of the RPA, 1950.
63.x: I and II are correct: the RPA, 1950 links to Articles 81, 82, 170, 171, 325 and 326, and the 1951 Act to 84, 102, 173, 191, 324 and 329. III is false because Article 329 belongs with the 1951 Act.
63.tq: Match each Act to its Articles.
n: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 is connected with Articles 81, 82, 170, 171, 325, and 326 of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 is connected with Articles 84, 102, 173, 191, 324, and 329 of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xs: Statements **I and II only** are correct — option **(3)**.
III is wrong: **Article 329** belongs with the **RPA 1951**.
xa: RPA 1950 = **pre-election** framework — **voter rolls**.
RPA 1951 = **operational conduct** of elections and **candidature**.
**Art. 329(b)** = elections challenged only by **election petition**.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about disqualification and election bodies:
1. Disqualifications for membership of Parliament are dealt with in Article 102.
2. IIIDEM, which trains election managers, is an institute of the Department of Personnel and Training.
3. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the disqualification for conviction continues for six years after release.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Article 102 covers disqualifications for Parliament; Article 84 its qualifications.
Statement 2: Incorrect: IIIDEM belongs to the Election Commission of India.
Statement 3: Correct: under the RPA 1951 the disqualification continues for six years after release.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about elections law:
1. Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.
2. Election expense accounts are dealt with in Sections 80–81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
3. An election held after a legislature is dissolved before the expiry of its normal term is called a general election.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the ECI.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Sections 77–78 of the 1951 Act cover election expenses, not Sections 80–81.
Statement 3: Incorrect: such an election is a mid-term election.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about delimitation and reserved seats:
1. The Delimitation Commission is constituted under a notification of the Election Commission.
2. Reservation of one-third of seats for women under the 106th Amendment is linked to Article 334A.
3. Tirupati is the Lok Sabha constituency in Andhra Pradesh reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Delimitation Commission is constituted under an Act of Parliament.
Statement 2: Correct: Article 334A relates to the women's one-third reservation.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Araku is the ST-reserved constituency; Tirupati is SC-reserved.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about reserved seats:
1. In a constituency reserved for Scheduled Castes, all voters of the constituency can vote.
2. The 106th Amendment does not provide one-third reservation of seats for women.
3. The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly has 29 seats reserved for Scheduled Castes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: reserved constituencies have a common electorate open to all voters.
Statement 2: Incorrect: it does provide one-third reservation; what is not correct is that it operates immediately, as it begins only after the next census and delimitation.
Statement 3: Correct: Andhra Pradesh has 29 SC and 7 ST Assembly seats.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about reservation and election machinery:
1. The 104th Amendment extended reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under Article 334 up to 2030.
2. Under Section 78 of the RPA 1951, election expense accounts must be filed with the District Election Officer within 15 days.
3. The Election Commission has control over officers deployed on poll duty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the 104th Amendment (2019) extended SC/ST seat reservation to 2030 and ended Anglo-Indian nomination.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Section 78 requires expense accounts to reach the DEO within 30 days, not 15 days.
Statement 3: Correct: the Election Commission controls officers on poll duty and may transfer them or act against partisan conduct.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about party recognition and election notification:
1. For State Party recognition on seat share, a party needs three per cent of Assembly seats or three seats, whichever is more.
2. A party is eligible for National Party recognition if it is recognised as a State party in at least five States.
3. For a Lok Sabha general election, the notification under Section 14 of the RPA 1951 is issued by the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: one criterion is three per cent of Assembly seats or three seats, whichever is more.
Statement 2: Incorrect: State-party recognition in four or more States is the criterion, not five.
Statement 3: Correct: the President notifies Lok Sabha polls on the ECI's recommendation.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about MCC and postal voting:
1. The authority of the Model Code of Conduct is associated with the Election Commission's plenary power under Article 324.
2. Persons in preventive detention may vote through a special booth in the jail.
3. The age threshold for senior citizens in the absentee-voter postal ballot category is 85 years or above.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Model Code is a set of ECI guidelines supported by Article 324, not a statute.
Statement 2: Incorrect: persons in preventive detention vote through postal ballot.
Statement 3: Correct: the senior-citizen threshold is 85 years or above, raised from 80 years.

63.s: Which of the following ECI initiative – purpose pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: SVEEP – Voter education and electoral participation
cVIGIL – Assistance and facilities for voters with disabilities
Saksham – Assistance and facilities for voters with disabilities
Voter Helpline – Registration, corrections, roll search and complaints
63.x: cVIGIL is for reporting Model Code violations through geo-tagged photographs or videos; Saksham assists voters with disabilities.
xa: cVIGIL promises action within **100 minutes**.
SVEEP was launched in **2009**; the ECI partnered **Indian Railways** (APPSC **2019**).
**ECINET** merges **40+** ECI apps and websites.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about elections and representation:
1. The grounds for declaring an election void are listed in Section 100 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
2. The 17th Lok Sabha was elected in 2019.

63.s: How many Delimitation Commissions have been constituted by the Government of India till December 2023?
63.x: Delimitation means the process of fixing the number of seats and boundaries of territorial constituencies in each State/UT for the Lok Sabha and Legislative assemblies. It also includes determining the seats to be reserved for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in these Houses. The 'delimitation process' in India is performed by the 'Delimitation Commission' that is set up under an Act of Parliament. In India, such Delimitation Commissions have been constituted 4 timesin 1952 under the Delimitation Commission Act, 1952, in 1963 under the Delimitation Commission Act, 1962, in 1973 under the Delimitation Act, 1972 and in 2002 under the Delimitation Act, 2002. The delimitation of four north-eastern States by the Delimitation Commission of 2002 (Chairman-Justice Kuldip Singh) was deferred due to security risks, by four separate presidential orders, all issued on 8 February 2008, for Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Manipur. The orders regarding these States were rescinded on 28 February 2020. Subsequently, the Government of India has again constituted the Delimitation Commission under the Section 3 of the Delimitation Act, 2002 for these four States as well as the UT of Jammu and Kashmir on 6 March 2020, under the chairpersonship of Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai. In March 2021, the four north-eastern States were removed from the purview of the reconstituted Commission. Hence, technically 5 Delimitation Commissions were constituted (including the 2020 Commission

Goswami also recommended **public funding** of elections.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about committees and election law:
1. The Indrajit Gupta Committee was not concerned with Centre-State relations.
2. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the ban on exit polls is provided in Section 123.
3. Disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the Speaker or Chairman, subject to judicial review by the courts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with state funding of elections, unlike Rajamannar, Sarkaria and Punchhi.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the ban on exit polls is in Section 126A, not Section 123.
Statement 3: Correct: the Speaker's or Chairman's decision remains subject to judicial review, as the Supreme Court recognised in 1992.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about State funding of elections:
1. The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) recommended State funding of elections in the form of partial cash funding to independents only.
2. The Law Commission's 170th Report found full state funding of elections desirable only if parties were barred from taking funds from other sources.
3. The 'level field for resource-poor candidates' argument for State funding of elections rests on equality under Article 21.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: it suggested partial funding in kind to recognised parties and candidates.
Statement 2: Correct: the Law Commission considered full state funding desirable only if parties were barred from other funds.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the level-field argument rests on equality under Article 14, not Article 21.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about election finance and counting:
1. In State of Karnataka v. Prathik Parasrampuria (2026), the Supreme Court described eliminating black money from elections as a core responsibility of the Election Commission of India.
2. A totaliser, which combines the counting of several EVMs, is intended to verify VVPAT slips.
3. The use of 'totalisers' in counting votes was recommended by the Indrajit Gupta Committee, 1998.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Court called eliminating black money from elections a core responsibility of the ECI.
Statement 2: Incorrect: a totaliser combines several EVM counts to conceal booth-wise voting trends.
Statement 3: Incorrect: totalisers were recommended by the Law Commission's 255th Report (2015); the Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with state funding.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about Indian electoral reforms:
1. Simultaneous Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections were held from 1951-52 up to 1967.
2. The High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections (2023-24) was chaired by Ram Nath Kovind.
3. A candidate forfeits the security deposit on failing to secure more than one-sixth of the total valid votes polled.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Correct: simultaneous polls were held from 1951-52 to 1967.
Statement 2: Correct: former President Ram Nath Kovind chaired the committee; Amit Shah and N.K. Singh were members.
Statement 3: Correct: a candidate loses the security deposit if they win no more than one-sixth of the valid votes.

64.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sarkaria Commission – Recommendation for a permanent Inter-State Council
Indrajit Gupta Committee – State funding of elections
Rajamannar Committee – State-level initiative for federal autonomy
Punchhi Commission – State-level initiative for federal autonomy
64.x: Punchhi dealt with federal dialogue and coordination mechanisms; the State-level autonomy initiative was Rajamannar (Tamil Nadu).
n: The Sarkaria Commission recommended establishing a permanent Inter-State Council or Inter-Governmental Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 70-72]
The Indrajit Gupta Committee concerned state funding of elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 70-72]
Federal dialogue and coordination mechanisms were the exam focus for the Punchhi Commission. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 70-72]
The Rajamannar Committee represented a state-level initiative for federal autonomy. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 70-72]
Punchhi Commission is categorized under federalism, Centre–State Relations, and coordination and dialogue mechanisms. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 70-72]
The Indrajit Gupta Committee is a classic elimination option under Centre–State questions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 70-72]
The recommendation for a permanent Inter-State Council or Inter-Governmental Council belongs to the Sarkaria Commission, not the Punchhi Commission. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 70-72]
xa: ⚠ The permanent ISC recommendation is **Sarkaria's**, **not** Punchhi's.
Years: Rajamannar **1969-71**; Sarkaria **1983-88** (**247** recommendations); Punchhi **2007-10**; Indrajit Gupta **1998**.
"Which is NOT on Centre-State relations?" → **Indrajit Gupta Committee** (APPSC-G2 2025).

64.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the death of a contesting candidate?
o: The election is automatically cancelled in every case of the death of a candidate.
The death of a candidate no longer automatically countermands the election.
The change was made through the 1996 Amendment.
Recognized political parties may nominate a replacement within a set timeframe.
64.x: Option A is incorrect: since the 1996 amendment, a candidate's death no longer cancels the election automatically. A recognised party can name a replacement within a set time.
64.tq: Recall the 1996 change on a candidate's death.
n: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 was amended in 1996 to cap the number of constituencies a candidate could contest at two. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
Before the 1996 amendment, elections were automatically countermanded upon the death of a contesting candidate. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
After the 1996 amendment, elections are no longer automatically countermanded upon the death of a contesting candidate. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
Recognized political parties may nominate a replacement for a deceased contesting candidate within a set timeframe. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the election is **automatically cancelled** on every candidate's death — option **(1)**.
After the **1996 amendment**, death **no longer** automatically countermands the election.
A **recognised political party** may **nominate a replacement** within a set timeframe.
xa: **Countermanding** now happens only on the death of a **recognised-party** candidate.
The **1996** Act also made poll day a **paid holiday** (**Sec. 135B**) and banned liquor **48 hours** before poll (**Sec. 135C**).
Bypolls within **6 months** (**Sec. 151A**).

64.s:
Consider the following statements about electoral reform committees and RPA:
1. The Dinesh Goswami Committee recommended State funding of elections and the use of Electronic Voting Machines, but not the allocation of State Legislative Council seats.
2. Under Section 33 of the RPA 1951, a candidate for the Lok Sabha or a State Assembly can contest from a maximum of two constituencies.
3. The Ram Nath Kovind High-Level Committee recommended holding Lok Sabha and Assembly elections together first, followed by local-body elections within 100 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Goswami Committee recommended State funding and EVMs; Council seat allocation was not its subject.
Statement 2: Correct: under Section 33(7), added in 1996, a candidate can contest from at most two constituencies.
Statement 3: Correct: the committee recommended joint Lok Sabha and Assembly polls first, then local-body elections within 100 days.

64.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the RPA, 1951 is correctly matched?
64.x: Section 33A concerns disclosure of criminal antecedents; Section 8 is disqualification on conviction, 29A registration of parties and 123 corrupt practices.
xa: **Sec. 34** = security deposit; **Sec. 81** = petition within **45 days**.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about the Representation of the People Act:
1. Failure to file an election expenditure account within 30 days is not among the corrupt practices covered by Section 123 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
2. The reform principle 'one candidate, one seat' addresses the criminalisation of politics.
3. A major provision of the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 1996 was the reduction of security deposits and proposers for independent candidates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Section 123 covers bribery, undue influence and appeals based on religion or caste; filing the expenditure account is governed by Section 78.
Statement 2: Incorrect: 'one candidate, one seat' addresses candidates contesting from more than one constituency, not the criminalisation of politics.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the 1996 amendment capped contests at two constituencies, increased security deposits and required more proposers for independents.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about RPA 1951 provisions:
1. A person elected from two constituencies must vacate one of them within 60 days.
2. Under Section 8 of the RPA 1951, conviction resulting in imprisonment of two years or more attracts disqualification.
3. Section 77 of the RPA 1951 is criticised because it places a ceiling only on candidates' expenditure, not on the election expenditure incurred directly by political parties.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: under Section 70 one seat must be vacated within 14 days, not 60 days.
Statement 2: Correct: Section 8 disqualifies on conviction with two years' imprisonment or more.
Statement 3: Correct: Section 77 caps candidate expenditure but imposes no comparable ceiling on the parties' own election spending.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about election expense accounts:
1. Section 77 of the RPA 1951 requires a candidate to keep an account of election expenses.
2. Section 78 requires the account to be filed with the Returning Officer within 30 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sec. 77 requires the candidate to keep expense accounts. Statement 2 is wrong: under Sec. 78 the account is filed with the District Election Officer, not the Returning Officer, within 30 days. So A; B and C accept the wrong statement 2, D rejects the correct statement 1.
64.tq: 77 = keep accounts, 78 = file with DEO in 30 days.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
**Sec. 77** requires keeping **expense accounts**.
Statement 2 is wrong: under **Sec. 78** the account goes to the **District Election Officer** within **30 days**, not the Returning Officer.
xa: Failure → the **ECI** can **disqualify** the candidate.
Limits rest on **Rule 90** of the **1961** Rules.

64.s:
Assertion (A): The ceiling on the number of constituencies from which a candidate may contest was introduced through an amendment to the RPA, 1951 in 1996.
Reason (R): The amendment followed the 1991 election in which Devi Lal contested from three Lok Sabha seats.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
64.x: Both are true: the 1996 amendment capped contests at two constituencies after Devi Lal stood from three Lok Sabha seats in 1991. R explains A.
64.tq: Recall the Devi Lal case behind the 1996 cap.
n: Devi Lal contested from three Lok Sabha seats in the 1991 elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 was amended in 1996 to cap the number of constituencies a candidate could contest at two. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
The **1996** amendment capped contests at **two** constituencies because **Devi Lal** had contested **three Lok Sabha seats** in **1991**.
xa: Before **1996** there was **no cap** (UPSC 2021 key).
Provision: **Section 33(7), RPA 1951**.
Winner of both must vacate one within **14 days** (**Sec. 70**).

64.s:
Consider the following statements about landmark electoral judgments:
1. Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013) held that a convicted legislator is disqualified immediately, without protection during the pendency of an appeal.
2. Mandatory disclosure by candidates of criminal cases, assets, liabilities and education was laid down in Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India.
3. In ADR v Union of India (2024), the Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme mainly because it violated the voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Lily Thomas held that conviction leads to immediate disqualification and an appeal gives no protection against it.
Statement 2: Incorrect: such disclosure was made mandatory by ADR v. Union of India (2002), not Public Interest Foundation.
Statement 3: Correct: the five-judge bench unanimously held that donor anonymity violated voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a).

64.s:
Consider the following statements about EVMs and VVPATs:
1. ECIL, one of the two public sector undertakings that manufacture EVMs, is headquartered in Pune.
2. Under ADR v. ECI (2024), symbol-loading units are to be sealed and preserved for 45 days.
3. Subramanian Swamy v ECI held that VVPAT is necessary for free and fair elections and directed its introduction in phases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: ECIL is headquartered in Hyderabad, not Pune; BEL is based in Bengaluru.
Statement 2: Correct: the Court ordered SLUs preserved for 45 days and allowed runners-up to seek checking of 5% of EVMs.
Statement 3: Correct: in Subramanian Swamy v ECI (2013) the Supreme Court held VVPAT necessary for free and fair polls and required its phased introduction.

64.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Supreme Court's position on EVMs is NOT correct?
o: In ADR v ECI (2024), the Court refused to order a return to paper ballots.
The Supreme Court has repeatedly upheld the use of EVMs.
In ADR v ECI (2024), the Court ordered a return to paper ballots.
The Court has considered safeguards relating to VVPAT verification.
64.x: The Supreme Court refused to order a return to paper ballots in ADR v ECI (2024). The other statements correctly reflect the Court's approach to EVMs and verification safeguards.
64.tq: Identify the reversed judicial conclusion in the NOT question.
xs: The NOT-correct statement: "ADR v ECI **ordered a return to paper ballots**" — option **(3)**.
In fact **ADR v ECI (2024)** **refused** a return to paper ballots; the SC has **repeatedly upheld EVMs**.
xa: It also rejected **100% slip counting**.
ECI admitted EVMs "are still a subject of frequent public questioning" (**2 Sep 2026**).

64.s:
Consider the following statements about NOTA:
1. In PUCL v Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court traced the right to reject to Article 19(1)(a).
2. NOTA was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2013.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x: Statement 1 is correct: PUCL (2013) linked the right to reject to Article 19(1)(a). Statement 2 is wrong: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly elections; its first Lok Sabha use was in 2014. So A; B and C accept the wrong statement 2, D rejects the correct statement 1.
64.tq: NOTA: 2013 Assembly polls first, 2014 first Lok Sabha.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
**PUCL (2013)** traced the right to reject to **Art. 19(1)(a)**.
Statement 2 is wrong: NOTA's first Lok Sabha use was **2014**; **2013** was the Assembly elections.
xa: In **2014** NOTA got **1.1%** (over **60 lakh** votes).
NOTA button added on **27 Sept 2013**.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about criminalisation and money in elections:
1. Under Section 34 of the RPA 1951, the security deposit for a general-category Lok Sabha candidate is ₹50,000.
2. Among the judgments on criminalisation of politics, it is not correct that Public Interest Foundation (2018) ordered publicity of candidates' criminal records.
3. Under the ECI's requirement, political parties fielding candidates with criminal records must publish the details of those records and the reasons for selecting such candidates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the deposit is ₹25,000 for the Lok Sabha, not ₹50,000; it is ₹10,000 for an Assembly.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the statement that is not correct is that in Public Interest Foundation (2018) the Court itself imposed disqualification on framing of charges; it left that issue to Parliament.
Statement 3: Correct: parties must publish the criminal-record details and the reasons for selecting such candidates.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about criminalisation and election finance:
1. Barring candidates upon framing of charges in serious offences was recommended by the Law Commission's 244th Report, 2014.
2. The current election expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in a larger State is ₹95 lakh.
3. To retain tax exemption, a political party must accept no cash donation above ₹2,000 and keep proper records of donations above ₹20,000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the recommendation was made in the Law Commission's 244th Report of 2014.
Statement 2: Correct: the limit is ₹95 lakh (earlier ₹70 lakh), raised by the Conduct of Elections (Amendment) Rules, 2022.
Statement 3: Correct: the stated conditions are no cash donation above ₹2,000 and records for donations above ₹20,000.

64.s:
On criminalisation of politics, consider the following statements:
1. A PIL seeking a lifetime ban on convicted legislators is pending.
2. 12 special courts have been set up for cases involving MPs and MLAs.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
64.x: A PIL seeking a lifetime ban on convicted legislators is pending, and 12 special courts have been established for cases involving MPs and MLAs.
xa: ADR: **31%** MPs, **29%** MLAs with serious charges.
Unfinished agenda: disqualification on **framing of charges**.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about electoral judgments and politics:
1. The Supreme Court's decision in ADR v. Union of India also invalidated the abolition of political party registration under the RPA.
2. N. Chandrababu Naidu v Union of India (2019) changed the random VVPAT-EVM tally from one to five polling stations per Assembly segment.
3. The expression "bahubali culture" refers primarily to the erosion of trust in legislatures through muscle power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Court struck down the removal of the corporate donation cap from the Companies Act, not any abolition of party registration.
Statement 2: Correct: the 2019 decision raised the random tally from one to five polling stations per Assembly segment.
Statement 3: Correct: the expression refers to muscle power and its adverse effect on trust in legislatures.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about election funding and electoral bonds:
1. The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended partial state funding and barring persons charged with serious offences.
2. A political party could encash electoral bonds only if it had secured at least 1 per cent of the votes in the last election.
3. In the 2024 electoral bond judgment, the Supreme Court directed the State Bank of India to provide donor data to the Election Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Second ARC recommended partial state funding and barring persons charged with serious offences.
Statement 2: Correct: only a registered party with at least 1% of the votes in the last election could encash electoral bonds.
Statement 3: Correct: the Constitution Bench struck down the scheme and directed SBI to provide donor data to the ECI.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about electoral bonds:
1. They were sold only by the State Bank of India.
2. They were issued in denominations from ₹1,000 to ₹10 crore.
3. They were bearer bonds valid for 15 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: Statement 1 is correct: SBI was the only seller. Statement 2 is wrong: the range was ₹1,000 to ₹1 crore. Statement 3 is correct: they were bearer bonds valid for 15 days. So C; A, B and D all include the wrong statement 2.
64.tq: Bonds: SBI only, ₹1,000-₹1 crore, 15 days, encashable by parties with 1% votes.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Electoral bonds were sold **only by SBI**, as **bearer bonds** valid **15 days**.
Statement 2 is wrong: denominations ran from **₹1,000 to ₹1 crore**, not ₹10 crore.
xa: The scheme was notified in **2018** (via Finance Act **2017** amendments).
Only parties with at least **1%** of the vote in the last election could encash them.
Struck down in **ADR v UoI** on **15 Feb 2024**.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about election funding and reforms:
1. A State funding model in which the State bears all legitimate costs and private donations are banned is full funding.
2. VVPAT slips must be counted whenever EVM data and Form 17C do not match.
3. A proposed safeguard for governmental accountability under simultaneous elections is based on the German model of a constructive vote of no-confidence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Correct: bearing all legitimate costs while banning private donations describes full funding.
Statement 2: Correct: VVPAT slips must be counted wherever EVM data and Form 17C do not match.
Statement 3: Correct: the proposed safeguard is a constructive no-confidence motion modelled on the German system.

64.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 2013 — Lily Thomas judgment striking down Section 8(4) of the RPA
2002 — Disclosure of criminal record, assets and education
64.x: Electoral bonds were struck down by the Supreme Court in 2024; they were not introduced in that year. The other pairs are correctly matched.
64.tq: Find the reversed action-year pair, particularly where a later year records invalidation rather than introduction.
xs: **2024 — Introduction of electoral bonds** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Electoral bonds were notified in **2018** and **struck down** in **2024** (**ADR v UoI**, **15 Feb 2024**).
The rest are correct: **Lily Thomas** struck down **Sec. 8(4)** in **2013**; **ADR v UoI** (**2002**) mandated disclosure; **EVMs** in all constituencies in **2004**.
xa: ⚠ **ADR v UoI** **2002** = disclosure; **2024** = electoral bonds; **ADR v ECI** **2024** = EVM/VVPAT.
Bonds were sold only by **SBI**, in **₹1,000 to ₹1 crore** denominations, valid **15 days**.
The verdict was by a unanimous **five-judge Constitution Bench**, under the **right to information** (**Art. 19(1)(a)**).

64.s:
Consider the following statements about Indian electoral machinery:
1. Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 relates to the registration of political parties.
2. Kerala was the first State to conduct its entire Assembly election using EVMs.
3. The Electors' Photo Identity Card (EPIC) was introduced in 1993.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Section 81 concerns election petitions presented in the High Court within 45 days of the result, not party registration.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Goa, not Kerala, conducted the first whole-State Assembly election using EVMs, in 1999.
Statement 3: Correct: EPIC was introduced in 1993 and its number stays valid for life.

64.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Section 135B — Liquor ban for 48 hours before polling
Section 135C — Paid holiday on polling day
Section 70 — Disqualification under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
64.x: Section 151A concerns holding a by-election within six months. Section 135B provides for a paid holiday, Section 135C concerns the liquor ban, and Section 70 deals with vacating one of two seats.
64.tq: Match statutory sections with their functions and eliminate the swapped-section pairs.
xs: **Sec. 151A — by-election within six months** is correct — option **(3)**.
**135B** = **paid holiday**; **135C** = **liquor ban** (pairs 1 and 2 are swapped).
**Sec. 70** = vacating one of two seats within **14 days**, not the National Honour Act disqualification.
xa: Bypoll exceptions: remaining term **under one year**, or ECI certifies difficulty.
National Honour Act is of **1971**.

64.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in relation to the constitutional provisions discussed in connection with simultaneous elections?
o: Article 83 — Duration of Houses of Parliament
Article 85 — Dissolution and related parliamentary matters
Article 174 — Dissolution and related matters concerning State Legislatures
Article 356 — Appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner
64.x: Article 356 concerns President's Rule, not appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner. Articles 83, 85 and 174 were among the provisions mentioned in the debate in relation to duration or dissolution.
64.tq: Use the wrong constitutional subject to identify the incorrectly matched pair.
xs: **Article 356 — appointment of the CEC** is wrong — option **(4)**; Art. **356** is **President's Rule**.
**83** = House duration; **85** and **174** = dissolution matters.
xa: The **CEC and ECs Act 2023** sets the CEC selection panel: **PM, a Cabinet Minister, LoP**.
The 129th Bill inserts **Art. 82A**.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about electoral rolls and the ECI:
1. Linking of electoral rolls with Aadhaar to check multiple enrolment was provided by the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021.
2. Under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, the selection panel consists of the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition.
3. The nationwide rollout of Electors Photo Identity Cards was initiated in 1993 under CEC T.N. Seshan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the 2021 Act provided Aadhaar linking, multiple qualifying dates and gender-neutral wording.
Statement 2: Correct: the 2023 Act provides this panel; the Chief Justice of India was dropped from it.
Statement 3: Correct: the nationwide EPIC rollout began in 1993 under CEC T.N. Seshan.

64.s:
Assertion (A): A registered elector in India can contest a Rajya Sabha election from any State.
Reason (R): The 2003 Amendment removed the requirement that the candidate be an elector in the particular State.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
64.x: Both are true: since a 2003 amendment removed the rule that a candidate must be a voter in that State, any registered voter in India can contest a Rajya Sabha seat from any State. R explains A.
64.tq: Recall the 2003 change upheld in Kuldip Nayar.
n: The 2003 amendment removed the requirement that a Rajya Sabha candidate be an elector in the particular State of contest. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
Any registered elector in India can contest a Rajya Sabha election from any State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
The **2003 amendment** removed the rule that a **Rajya Sabha** candidate be an **elector** in that **particular State**, so any **registered elector** in India can contest from **any State**.
xa: Upheld by the **Supreme Court** in **Kuldip Nayar** (**2006**).
Before **2003**, domicile/voter requirement applied.
**1996** changes: cap of **two constituencies**, higher deposits.

64.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
64.x: VVPAT was introduced on 4 September 2013; EVMs were first used on 19 May 1982, EPIC rolled out in 1993 and NOTA on 27 September 2013.
n: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) were first used experimentally on 19 May 1982. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
Electors Photo Identity Cards (EPICs) had their nationwide rollout initiated in 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) was first used on 4 September 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
None of the Above (NOTA) was implemented on 27 September 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
VVPAT was introduced before NOTA in 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
NOTA was mandated later in September 2013 than VVPAT was introduced. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xa: ⚠ **VVPAT** came **before NOTA** in **2013**.
**Section 61A** (RPA 1951) gave EVMs statutory backing in **1989**.
**2004** = first all-EVM Lok Sabha election.

64.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Goa (1999) – First State-wide Assembly election using EVMs
Parur Assembly Constituency – First experimental use of EVM
14th Lok Sabha election (2004) – First nationwide general election entirely using EVMs
64.x: VVPAT was first introduced in Noksen Assembly Constituency; Goa saw the first all-EVM State poll.
n: The first experimental use of EVMs occurred in the Parur Assembly Constituency in Kerala. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The first VVPAT use occurred in the Noksen Assembly Constituency in Nagaland. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
Goa was the first State to conduct an entire General Assembly election using EVMs across all constituencies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The 14th Lok Sabha General Election in 2004 was the first nationwide general election conducted entirely using EVMs. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xa: ⚠ **Gujarat** was **not** the first State to use EVMs in an Assembly election.
Noksen VVPAT use was a **by-election** on **4 September 2013**.
EVM makers: **BEL** (Bengaluru) and **ECIL** (Hyderabad).

64.s: Section 61A was inserted into the Representation of the People Act, 1951, in which year to provide statutory backing to Electronic Voting Machines?

66.s: Which one of the following statements regarding political parties and the Constitution of India, as originally adopted, is correct?

xs: The Constitution as adopted **said nothing about political parties** — it **contained no specific provision** on them — so option **(2)** is correct.
It neither recognised only national parties nor prescribed a two-party or coalition system.
xa: Parties first entered the Constitution via the **anti-defection law** (**Tenth Schedule**, **52nd Amendment, 1985**).
India has a **multi-party system**, unlike the two-party **UK** and **USA**.
Parties are classed by ECI status as **national**, **state** and **registered-unrecognised**.

n: The Election Commission of India registers political parties under the Representation of the People Act, 1951. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India allots election symbols under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India decides recognition of political parties under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India adjudicates disputes concerning party mergers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India adjudicates disputes concerning party splits. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
