This aligns with Article 29 of the UDHR, which asserts that everyone has duties to the community and that the exercise of rights and f

125.s: Which statement is true in relation to the Protection of Human Rights Act?
o: The Act came into force on 23rd September, 1993
The Act came into force on 28th September, 1993
The Act came into force on 23rd September, 1995
The Act came into force on 28th September, 1995
125.x: The Protection of Human Rights Act came into force on the 28th Day of September 1993. It extends to the whole of India.

125.s: When did the Protection of Human Rights Act come into force in India?
125.x: On 28 September, 1993, the Human Rights Protection Act came into force in India. It protects and promotes Human Rights.

125.s: In the definition of armed forces under the Protection of Human Rights Act, which of the following is not included?
125.x: Under the Act, 'armed forces' means the naval, military and air force and includes other armed forces of the Union. Hence Armed Forces of the State are not included in the Act.

125.s: Which of the following rights is not under the purview of the National Human Rights Commission ?
125.x: Section 2(M) of the Human Rights Protection Act, 1993 defines ‘Public Servant’. It shall have the same meaning assigned to the term under Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

125.s: Every member of the Commission, Sate Commission and every officer appointed or authorized by the Commission or State Commission to exercise functions under the Protection of Human Rights Act is to be deemed
125.x: Every member of the Commission, State Commission and every officer appointed or authorised by the Commission or State Commission to exercise functions under the Protection of Human Rights Act is to be deemed a Public Servant. It is as per the legal definition of Public Servant (Section 21 of IPC)

125.s: An advocate may be specified by the State Government for the purpose of conducting of cases in Human Rights courts as Special Public Prosecutor who has been in practice for not less than :
125.x: Under section 31 in the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, a Special Public Prosecutor for every Human Rights court, the State government shall, by notification, specify a public prosecutor or appoint an advocate who has been in practice as an advocate for not less than 7 years, as a Special Public Prosecutor for the purpose of conducting cases in that court.

125.s: Which of the following is not a Social Act?
125.x: The Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) was enacted in 1971 and was repealed in 1977. This Act was enacted for the maintenance of internal security. Thus, it is not a Social Act, while the other three mentioned Acts were enacted for prevention of social evils.

125.s: Bonded Labour was abolished in India, by an Act of Parliament enacted in the year –
125.x: Article 23(1) of the Constitution prohibits the traffic in human beings and forced labour. Any contravention of this provision shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law. The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Ordinance, 1975 was promulgated by the President on 25 October, 1975. To replace the said Ordinance, the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Bill, 1976 was introduced in the Parliament. The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Bill, 1976 was passed by both the Houses of Parliament, and it became an Act in 1976.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission:
1. The National Human Rights Commission is a statutory body created under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
2. The establishment of the NHRC conforms to the Delhi Declaration.
3. M.N. Venkatachaliah was the first Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the NHRC is a statutory body under the PHRA, 1993, not a constitutional body.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the NHRC was established in conformity with the Paris Principles.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Justice Ranganath Misra was the first Chairperson of the NHRC.

126.s: Which one of the following statements about constituting a State Human Rights Commission is correct?
o: An SHRC can be constituted only by Parliament through a constitutional amendment.
A State Government may constitute an SHRC under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
Every State Government is constitutionally required to constitute an SHRC.
Only the NHRC can constitute an SHRC.
126.x: Constitution of an SHRC is optional; the State Government may constitute one under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
126.tq: Test the significance of the word ‘may’ by contrasting an optional power with a mandatory duty.
xs: A **State Government "may" constitute an SHRC** under the **PHRA, 1993** — option **(2)**.
Constituting an SHRC is **optional** — not a constitutional duty, and neither Parliament nor the NHRC creates it.
xa: SHRC chair: former **HC Chief Justice or Judge**; **three** members.
SHRC members are **appointed by the Governor** but **removable only by the President**.
Criticism: **optional creation**, advisory powers and **vacancies** weaken SHRCs.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the NHRC and the Paris Principles:
1. The Paris Principles establish the jurisdiction of State Human Rights Commissions over Union Territories.
2. The NHRC is a statutory body, whereas the UPSC and CAG are constitutional bodies.
3. In 1997, the Supreme Court entrusted the NHRC with monitoring the implementation of the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Paris Principles set standards of independence, pluralism and a broad mandate for national human-rights institutions.
Statement 2: Correct: the NHRC is statutory, while the UPSC and the CAG are constitutional bodies.
Statement 3: Correct: in 1997 the Supreme Court entrusted the NHRC with monitoring the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976.

126.s:
Assertion (A): After the 2019 amendment, the NHRC has seven deemed members.
Reason (R): The 2019 amendment added the Chairpersons of the NCBC and NCPCR and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities to the four existing deemed members.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
126.x: Adding these three heads to the four earlier deemed members made seven, so R explains A.
xa: Deemed members before 2019: chairpersons of **NCM, NCSC, NCST, NCW**.
**NCSC and NCST** chairpersons were themselves added by the **2006** amendment.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the NHRC:
1. The NHRC includes three persons having knowledge of human rights, at least one of whom must be a woman.
2. A deemed member of the NHRC is not identical in status to an ordinary NHRC member.
3. A sitting Judge of the Supreme Court or a sitting Chief Justice of a High Court can be appointed to the NHRC only after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the NHRC includes three, not two, persons with knowledge of human rights, at least one a woman.
Statement 2: Correct: the deemed-member provision does not convert the Chairpersons into ordinary NHRC members.
Statement 3: Correct: such an appointment requires consultation with the Chief Justice of India.

126.s: Which one of the following statements about the pre-2019 and post-2019 composition of the NHRC is correct?
o: The number of human-rights experts fell from three to two after 2019.
Before 2019, only a former CJI was eligible as Chairperson; after 2019, a Supreme Court Judge was also included.
Before 2019, the Chairperson could be any Supreme Court Judge, but after 2019 only the former CJI was eligible.
The number of deemed members fell from seven to four after 2019.
126.x: Before 2019, the Chairperson had to be a former Chief Justice of India. After 2019, a Judge of the Supreme Court was also eligible; the number of human-rights experts and deemed members increased.
126.tq: Compare the direction of each amendment and reject options that reverse the change.
xs: Before **2019** only a former **CJI** could chair; after 2019 a **Judge of the Supreme Court** is also eligible — option **(2)**.
Option (3) reverses this; human-rights experts **rose** from two to three and deemed members **rose** from **4** to **7**.
xa: The term changed from **5 years or 70** to **3 years or 70**.
SHRC chair widened from HC **Chief Justice** only to **CJ or Judge** of a High Court.
The **5-year reappointment limit** was removed.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about NHRC members' tenure and removal:
1. A member of the NHRC resigns by writing addressed to the Prime Minister.
2. For removal of the NHRC Chairperson on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, the President refers the matter to the Supreme Court.
3. After demitting office, the Chairperson or a member of the NHRC is ineligible for further employment under the Central or any State Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: an NHRC Chairperson or member resigns in writing addressed to the President of India.
Statement 2: Correct: the President refers such cases to the Supreme Court for inquiry.
Statement 3: Correct: they are not eligible for further employment under the Central or any State Government.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about appointing and removing Commission heads:
1. The Chief Justice of India is not a member of the Prime Minister-headed committee that recommends NHRC appointments.
2. The Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission can be removed only by the President.
3. The selection committee for a State Human Rights Commission is headed by the Chief Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the committee is the PM, Lok Sabha Speaker, Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman, both Leaders of Opposition and the Home Minister; the CJI is only consulted.
Statement 2: Correct: the Governor appoints the SHRC Chairperson, but only the President can remove them.
Statement 3: Correct: the Chief Minister chairs it, with the Speaker, State Home Minister and Leader of Opposition.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about State Human Rights Commissions:
1. After the 2006 amendment, a State Human Rights Commission consists of four members, including the Chairperson.
2. A State Human Rights Commission inquires into violations relating to subjects in the State List and Concurrent List.
3. An SHRC will not inquire into a case already being inquired into by another statutory commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the 2006 amendment reduced it from five to three members, not four.
Statement 2: Correct: an SHRC covers the State and Concurrent Lists; the NHRC covers all subjects.
Statement 3: Correct: simultaneous inquiry into the same pending matter by the SHRC, NHRC or another statutory commission is barred.

126.s: Which of the following pairs relating to State Human Rights Commissions is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Inquiry powers – Same civil-court powers as the NHRC
126.x: An SHRC has no power to punish violators or enforce its recommendations as decrees; they are advisory.
xa: SHRC jurisdiction: subjects in the **State List** and **Concurrent List**.
The SHRC sends its **annual report** to the **State Government**; laid before the **State Legislature**.
"**Toothless tiger**" criticism: non-binding advice, one-year bar, armed-forces limit.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about NHRC jurisdiction and accreditation:
1. The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after one year from the date of the alleged act.
2. GANHRI accredits national human-rights institutions.
3. In the Gade Sai Krishna custodial-death case, the NHRC directed the Andhra Pradesh SHRC, DGP and Chief Secretary to submit a report.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the NHRC is barred after one year from the alleged act.
Statement 2: Correct: GANHRI accredits national human-rights institutions ('A' for fully compliant, 'B' for others).
Statement 3: Correct: the NHRC directed the AP SHRC, the Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary to report.

126.s: Which of the following statements regarding the NHRC's High-Level Selection Committee is incorrect?
o: The committee consists of six members, including the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Prime Minister is the Chairperson of the Selection Committee
The President of India appoints the NHRC based on the committee's recommendations
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is a member of the Selection Committee
126.x: Option D is incorrect: the Rajya Sabha's Deputy Chairman, not its Chairman, sits on the NHRC selection committee. The Prime Minister chairs the six-member committee, and the President appoints on its advice.
126.tq: Recall the NHRC selection committee's members.
n: The President of India appoints the NHRC Chairperson and members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The President of India makes appointments to the NHRC based on the recommendations of a six-member High-Level Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The Prime Minister is the Chairperson of the High-Level Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is a member of the High-Level Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is not a member of the High-Level Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The Deputy Chairman represents the Rajya Sabha on the High-Level Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is a member of the High-Level Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** is a committee member — option **(4)**.
The **Deputy Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha represents the House on the **six-member** committee.
The **Prime Minister** chairs it, the **Speaker** of the Lok Sabha sits on it, and the **President** appoints on its recommendation.
xa: Other members: **Union Home Minister**, **Leaders of the Opposition** in both Houses.
A **vacancy** in the committee does not invalidate its decisions.
SHRC committee is headed by the **Chief Minister**; SHRC members are **removable only by the President**.
First NHRC Chairperson: **Justice Ranganath Misra**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2019 PHRA amendment:
1. Under the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, reappointment of NHRC members needs a compulsory gap of five years.
2. The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 made members ineligible for reappointment.
3. The NHRC can intervene in court proceedings involving human-rights allegations with the approval of the court concerned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the 2019 amendment removed the earlier five-year limit, so reappointment is permitted.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the 2019 amendment removed the five-year limit, so members remain eligible for reappointment.
Statement 3: Correct: it needs the approval of the court concerned, not the Central Government.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about SHRC and NHRC powers:
1. The Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission resigns by writing addressed to the Governor and holds office for 3 years or till 70, whichever is earlier.
2. The 2006 amendment to the Protection of Human Rights Act enabled the NHRC to transfer complaints to the concerned SHRC.
3. The NHRC has the power to make binding recommendations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Correct: since 2006 the SHRC Chairperson resigns to the Governor, and since 2019 the term is 3 years or 70, whichever is earlier.
Statement 2: Correct: the 2006 amendment enabled the NHRC to transfer complaints to the concerned SHRC.
Statement 3: Incorrect: NHRC recommendations are advisory; its powers include visiting jails to study inmates' living conditions.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about NHRC powers and functions:
1. The NHRC may not inquire into a complaint solely against a private individual with no public servant involved.
2. While inquiring into complaints, the NHRC has the powers of a civil court.
3. The NHRC may recommend compensation and interim relief, including during the inquiry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the NHRC's jurisdiction concerns violations or negligence by public servants, so a purely private complaint is outside it.
Statement 2: Correct: the NHRC has civil-court powers such as summoning persons and requiring documents.
Statement 3: Correct: since the 2006 amendment, the NHRC may recommend interim relief even during the inquiry.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the NHRC and the AP SHRC:
1. Custodial deaths are required to be reported to the NHRC within 24 hours.
2. The Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission is constituted by the Andhra Pradesh Government under the PHRA, 1993.
3. The NHRC is criticised as a 'toothless tiger' mainly because its advice is non-binding.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Correct: custodial deaths are to be reported to the NHRC within 24 hours.
Statement 2: Correct: the AP SHRC is constituted by the Andhra Pradesh Government under the PHRA, 1993.
Statement 3: Correct: the criticism rests on its non-binding advice, along with the one-year bar and armed-forces limits.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about limits on NHRC action:
1. After the NHRC sends its inquiry report, the Government concerned must inform the Commission of the action taken within one month.
2. After the 2019 change, the Central Government may confer a Union Territory's human-rights functions on an SHRC, while Delhi's functions are handled by the NHRC.
3. While dealing with complaints against members of the armed forces, the NHRC may seek a report from the Central Government and make recommendations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Government must inform the Commission of the action taken within one month.
Statement 2: Correct: UT functions may be conferred on an SHRC; Delhi's are handled by the NHRC itself.
Statement 3: Correct: in armed-forces cases, the NHRC may seek a Central Government report and make recommendations.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about limits on Human Rights Commissions:
1. In cases concerning the armed forces, the Central Government must inform the NHRC of the action taken within one year.
2. NHRC recommendations are advisory, although the Government must respond to the Commission.
3. The annual report of a State Human Rights Commission is submitted to the State Government and then to the Governor alone for final approval.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Central Government must inform the NHRC within three months, not one year.
Statement 2: Correct: NHRC recommendations are advisory; the Government must inform the Commission of action taken.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the State Government lays the report before the State Legislature with a memorandum of action taken.

126.s: When was the Human Rights Commission of India constituted?
126.x: The National Human Rights Commission was constituted in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, establishing India's primary statutory body dedicated to investigating human rights violations.

126.s: According to the National Human Rights Commission Act, 1993, who amongst the following can be its chairman?
o: Any serving Judge of the Supreme Court
Any serving Judge of the High Court
Only a retired Chief Justice of India
Only a retired Chief Justice of High Court
126.x: Originally, the NHRC Chairperson had to be a retired Chief Justice of India. After the 2019 amendment, eligibility expanded to include any former Supreme Court Judge. Thus, appointment of serving judges or retired High Court Chief Justices is not allowed, and option 3 reflects the earlier rule but is no longer exclusively correct.

126.s:
Consider the following organisations/bodies in India:
1. The National Commission for Backward Classes
2. The National Human Rights Commission
3. The National Law Commission
4. The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
How many of the above are constitutional bodies?
126.x: The National Commission for Backward Classes is a constitutional body: It was set up in 1993 by an act of Parliament. The 102 nd Amendment Act of 2018 gave constitutional status to the. NCBC. The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is not a constitutional body: It is a statutory body constituted under the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993, which was later amended by the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA) 2006. The National Law Commission is not a constitutional body: The Law Commission of India (executive body) is a non-statutory body and is constituted by a notification of the Government of India, Ministry of Law and Justice, Department of Legal Affairs, with a definite set of terms of reference to carry out research in the field of law. The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission is not a constitutional body: It is a statutory body established in 1988 under the Consumer Protection Act (CPA) 1986. It is headed by a sitting or a retired Judge of the SC or a sitting or a retired CJHC. Jurisdiction: To entertain a complaint valued at more than two crores and Appellate and Revisional jurisdiction from the orders of the State Commissions or the District Commissions.

126.s: According to the National Human Rights Commission Act, 1993 who amongst the following can be its Chairman?
o: Any Serving Judge of the Supreme Court
Any Serving Judge of the High Court
Only a retired Chief Justice of India
Only a retired Chief Justice of a High Court
126.x: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India was established on 12 October, 1993. Justice Ranganath Misra was the first president of NHRC and his tenure in office was from 12 October, 1993 to 24 November, 1996.

126.s: Who presides over the committee constituted for the appointment of members of the State Human Rights Commission?
126.x: According to Section 22 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Chairperson and Members shall be appointed by the Governor after obtaining the recommendation of a Committee consisting of (a) the Chief Minister-chairperson; (b) Speaker of the Legislative Assembly-member, (c) Minister in-charge of the Department of Home in that Statemember; (d) Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly-member: and where there is a Legislative Council in a State, the Chairman of that Council and the Leader of the Opposition in that Council shall also be members of the Committee.

126.s: Who is not a member of the committee for the appointment of Chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission?
o: Speaker of the House of People
Chairman of the Council of States
Leader of opposition in the House of People
Leader of opposition in the Council of States
126.x: Section 4 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 lays down that the Chairperson and the members of the Commission are appointed by the President of India, on the recommendations of a Committee consisting of: The Prime Minister, the Speaker of the House of the People, Minister-in-charge of the Ministry of Home Affairs in the Government of India, leader of the Opposition in the House of the People, leader of the Opposition in the Council of States and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States. The chairman of the Council of States is not a member of the National Human Rights Commission.

126.s: Who is not a member of the committee constituted for recommendations of appointment of chairperson and other members of National Human Rights Commission?
o: Speaker of the House of the People
Leader of the Opposition in the House of the People
Chairman of the Council of States

126.s: The term of office of members of the National Human Rights Commission from the date on which he/she enters upon his/her office is
o: five years or till the age of 65 years
five years or till the age of 70 years
six years or till the age of 65 years
six years or till the age of 70 years
126.x: According to 'The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is to be headed by a former Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court. The Chairman of NHRC holds the office for 3 years or till he attains the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier. Thus Both (A) and (R) are wrong.

126.s: A Sitting Judge of the High Court or a Sitting District Judge can be appointed as a member of the State Human Rights Commission after consultation with?
o: the Chief Justice of the High Court of the concerned
the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India
126.x: The Protection of Human Rights Act 1993 provides for the creation of the State Human Rights Commission at the State level. Currently, 25 states have constituted the State Human Rights Commissions through official Gazette notifications. The Chairperson and members are appointed by the Governor on the recommendations of a committee consisting of the Chief Minister as its head, the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, the State's Home Minister and the leader of opposition. In case of a state having a Legislative Council the Chairman of the council and the leader of the opposition in the council would also be members of the committee. A Sitting Judge of a High Court or a sitting District Judge can be appointed only after consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court of the concerned state.

126.s: Chairperson and Members of the State Human Rights Commission are appointed by.
o: Chief Justice of the High Court of the concerned State

126.s: Chairperson and members of State Human Rights Commission are appointed by –
126.x: The State Human Rights Commission’s Chairman is appointed by the Governor. The Governor makes these appointments on the recommendation of a Committee comprising the Chief Minister (Chairman), Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, State Home Minister and the opposition leader of the Legislative Assembly (Members). In the case of a state having a Legislative Council, the chairman of the Council and the leader of the opposition in the council would also be members of the committee.

126.s: In the event of occurrence of any vacancy in the Office of the Chairperson of the State Commission, who can authorize one of the members to act as Chairperson?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
The Chairperson of the National Human Rights
126.x: The Governor can appoint one of the members of the State Commission as an acting chairman in the following two cases- (a) When the office of the Chairman falls vacant; (b) When the chairman is unable to perform his functions due to absence or some other reason.

126.s: Which one of the following is not the function of the State Human Rights Commission?
o: Enquire suo-moto the violation of Human Rights
Review the protection of Human Rights
To punish for the violation of Human Rights
126.x: All the above options are the functions of the Human Rights Commission except to punish for the violation of Human Rights.

126.s:
Analyze the statements with reference to National Human Rights Commission :
(i) The Human Rights Commission, encourages organizations working in the field of Human Rights.
(ii) The work of the Commission is also to conduct research in the field of Human Rights. Answer from the following.
o: Statement (i) is the correct explanation of Statement
126.x: The functions of the National Human Rights Commission have been given in section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The functions of the Commission include undertaking and promoting research in the field of human rights. The Commission also encourages the efforts of nongovernmental organisations and institutions working in the field of human rights. Hence both the statements are correct but statement II does not explain the statement I.

126.s: While dealing with complaints of violation of Human Rights by the members of the armed forces, the Commission either on its own motion or on receipt of a petition will?
o: give directions to the concerned police officers to
seek a report from the Central Government
126.x: The commission has limited role, powers and jurisdiction with respect to violation of Human rights by the members of the armed forces. In this sphere, the commission may seek a report from the central Government and make its recommendations.

126.s: The State Commission submits its annual report to the?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
126.x: The State Human Rights Commission submits its annual report to the State Government. The reports are laid before the State Legislature, along with a memorandum of action taken on the recommendations of the Commission and the reason for non-acceptance of any of such recommendations.

127.s: Which of the following case–principle pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Nilabati Behera – Compensation for custodial death
Joginder Kumar – Arrest must be justified; a relative may be informed
Arnesh Kumar – No automatic arrest for offences up to seven years
D.K. Basu – No automatic arrest for offences up to seven years
127.x: D.K. Basu laid down arrest safeguards like the arrest memo and medical examination; the seven-year rule is from Arnesh Kumar.
xa: ⚠ **1993 – 1994 – 1997 – 2014** = **Nilabati – Joginder – D.K. Basu – Arnesh**.
Arnesh Kumar's checklist: **CrPC s.41**, now **BNSS s.35**.
Nilabati compensation is under **Arts 32/226**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about Supreme Court rulings on policing:
1. Automatic arrest in every offence punishable up to seven years is not a safeguard associated with D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal.
2. The Supreme Court issued five directives on police reform in Prakash Singh v Union of India (2006).
3. The guidelines in PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) concerning encounter deaths consisted of 16 points.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x:
Statement 1: Correct: D.K. Basu required safeguards such as an arrest memo and medical examination; automatic arrest is contrary to the safeguard approach.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Prakash Singh (2006) issued seven directives, not five.
Statement 3: Correct: PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) laid down 16-point guidelines for encounter deaths.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about police reform and encounter guidelines:
1. Under the Prakash Singh (2006) directives, the DGP was to get a two-year tenure, not five years.
2. Under the Prakash Singh framework, the State Police Complaints Authority is headed by a retired judge.
3. Under the PUCL guidelines on encounter deaths, out-of-turn promotion or gallantry awards are barred until the officers involved are cleared.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the DGP was to be selected from a UPSC panel and given a two-year tenure, not five years.
Statement 2: Correct: the State PCA is headed by a retired judge and handles serious misconduct such as custodial death.
Statement 3: Correct: the guidelines prohibit out-of-turn promotion or gallantry awards until clearance.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about encounter deaths and mercy powers:
1. According to the NHRC, encounter deaths can be investigated only by the armed forces.
2. In Shatrughan Chauhan v. Union of India (2014), the Court held that inordinate, unexplained delay in deciding a mercy petition may justify commutation of a death sentence.
3. Epuru Sudhakar v. Government of Andhra Pradesh (2006) held that mercy powers are completely immune from judicial scrutiny.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the NHRC treats encounter deaths as serious violations requiring mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation.
Statement 2: Correct: the Court held that inordinate, unexplained delay may justify commutation of a death sentence.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Epuru Sudhakar (2006) held that pardon and remission are open to limited judicial review.

127.s: Which of the following pairs (case — holding) is correctly matched?
o: Bachan Singh (1980) — Categories of rarest cases
Machhi Singh (1983) — Death penalty held constitutional
Bachan Singh (1980) — 'Rarest of rare': life the rule, death the exception
127.x: Bachan Singh (1980) laid down 'rarest of rare'; Jagmohan Singh (1973) upheld the death penalty and Machhi Singh (1983) set categories of rarest cases.
xa: **Epuru Sudhakar (2006)**: pardon/remission open to limited **judicial review**.
**Shatrughan Chauhan (2014)**: inordinate delay → **commute to life**.
**Law Commission 262nd (2015)**: abolish except **terrorism and waging war**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about death sentences and torture law:
1. A death sentence passed by a Sessions Court must be confirmed by the Supreme Court.
2. An appeal against a death sentence may reach the Supreme Court under Articles 132, 134 and 136.
3. The 273rd Law Commission Report recommended ratification of UNCAT and a draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: a death sentence passed by a Sessions Court requires confirmation by the High Court, not the Supreme Court.
Statement 2: Correct: such appeals may lie to the Supreme Court under Articles 132, 134 and 136.
Statement 3: Correct: the 273rd Report (2017) recommended ratifying UNCAT and proposed a draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017.

127.s:
Assertion (A): The Governor cannot pardon a death sentence under Article 161.
Reason (R): The Governor may commute, remit or suspend a death sentence.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
127.x: Both are correct, but the Governor's power to commute or suspend does not explain why the Governor cannot pardon a death sentence.
xa: ⚠ **Art 72** = President can pardon death; **Art 161** = Governor cannot.
**Epuru Sudhakar (2006)**: pardon/remission open to limited **judicial review**.
**Shatrughan Chauhan (2014)**: delay in mercy → commutation.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about custodial deaths and torture:
1. CrPC Section 176(1A), now BNSS Section 196, made a judicial inquiry mandatory in cases of custodial death.
2. During 1999–2023, 2,253 police-custody deaths and 3 convictions were reported.
3. India signed the UN Convention against Torture (UNCAT), which it has not ratified, in 1997.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x:
Statement 1: Correct: CrPC Section 176(1A) made judicial inquiry mandatory; the BNSS equivalent is Section 196.
Statement 2: Correct: the data recorded 2,253 police-custody deaths and only three convictions during 1999–2023.
Statement 3: Correct: India signed UNCAT in 1997 but has not ratified it.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about prisons law in India:
1. Under the Seventh Schedule, prisons are included in Entry 4 of the State List.
2. The Model Prisons Act, 2023 guides States in replacing the colonial Prisons Act of 1894.
3. Under BNSS Section 479, an undertrial is generally eligible for release after serving one-fourth of the maximum term, or one-sixth for first-time offenders.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x:
Statement 1: Correct: prisons are a State subject under Entry 4 of the State List.
Statement 2: Correct: the Model Prisons Act, 2023 is meant to replace the Prisons Act, 1894.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Section 479 provides release after one-half of the maximum term, or one-third for first-time offenders.

127.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the administration of prisons is correct?
o: Prisons are governed exclusively by the Union Government under the Prisons Act, 1894.
The Supreme Court directly administers all prisons through BPR&D.
Prisons are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 and State jail manuals, while BPR&D issues advisory guidelines.
State jail manuals have no role after the enactment of the Model Prisons Act, 2023.
127.x: Prisons continue to be governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 and State jail manuals; BPR&D issues advisory guidelines.
127.tq: Identify the correct combination of governing law, State rules and advisory authority.
xs: Prisons are governed by the **Prisons Act 1894** and **State jail manuals**, while **BPR&D** issues **advisory guidelines** — option **(3)**.
Prisons are a **State List (Entry 4)** subject — not run by the Union or the Supreme Court.
The **Model Prisons Act 2023** is only a **guide** for States, so jail manuals still apply.
xa: The **Mulla Committee** (**1980-83**) sought a **national prison policy**.
NCRB **2024**: occupancy **112.7%**; undertrials **~73%**.
**SC (Aug 2025)**: immediate release of prisoners held beyond sentence.

127.s: Which committee focused on women prisoners and greater representation of women in the police?
127.x: The Krishna Iyer Committee dealt with women prisoners; Mulla covered comprehensive jail reforms and Amitava Roy overcrowding and undertrials.
xa: The Amitava Roy Committee was **SC-appointed**.
**Law Commission 262nd (2015)**: death penalty; **273rd (2017)**: torture.
Women are **4.14%** of inmates; only **34** women's prisons.

127.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the Law Commission report with its subject?
o: 262nd Report (2015) — abolition of the death penalty for all crimes except terrorism and waging war
273rd Report (2017) — classification of rarest-of-rare cases under Machhi Singh
262nd Report (2015) — ratification of UNCAT and draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017
273rd Report (2017) — creation of the All India Prison Service
127.x: The 262nd Report (2015) recommended abolishing the death penalty for all crimes except terrorism and waging war. The 273rd Report concerned UNCAT ratification and a draft anti-torture Bill.
127.tq: Discriminate between the two Law Commission reports by subject and year.
xs: **262nd Report (2015)** — abolish the death penalty for all crimes **except terrorism and waging war** — option **(1)**.
The **273rd (2017)** dealt with **UNCAT ratification** and a draft torture Bill; rarest-of-rare categories come from **Machhi Singh**; the All India Prison Service from the **Mulla Committee**.
xa: ⚠ **262nd** = death penalty; **273rd** = torture.
**Jagmohan Singh (1973)** held the death penalty constitutional.
**Shatrughan Chauhan (2014)**: **14 days** between mercy rejection and execution.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about custody and prison statistics:
1. Bihar records the highest number of deaths in police custody.
2. According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, undertrials constituted approximately 73% of inmates.
3. According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, the prison occupancy rate was 112.7% and undertrials made up 63% of inmates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Bihar records the most police-custody deaths, followed by Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
Statement 2: Correct: undertrials were about 73% of inmates.
Statement 3: Incorrect: occupancy was 112.7%, but undertrials were 73%, not 63%.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about prisoners, executions and custodial death:
1. Parole and furlough are governed by identical Central rules applicable to every State.
2. According to Amnesty International, China is the world's biggest state executioner.
3. Gade Sai Krishna's custodial-death case in Andhra Pradesh was associated with Krishnalanka police station, Vijayawada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: parole and furlough are not absolute rights, and each State frames its own prisoner-release rules.
Statement 2: Correct: China was identified as the world's biggest state executioner.
Statement 3: Correct: the case concerned the Krishnalanka police station in Vijayawada.

127.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Statement-I: In India, prisons are managed by State Governments with their own rules and regulations for the day-to-day administration of prisons.
2. Statement-II: In India, prisons are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 which expressly kept the subject of prisons in the control of Provincial Governments. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, and Statement-II is the correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
127.x: Answer is (a): 'Prisons' is a State subject under the State List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. The management and administration of Prisons fall exclusively within the domain of the State Governments and are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894, and the Prison Manuals of the respective State Governments. Thus, States have the primary role, responsibility, and authority to change current prison laws, rules, and regulations. Therefore, the Prisons Act of 1894 placed responsibility for prisons under the jurisdiction of Provincial governments (State governments), which explains why State governments have the authority to establish their own rules and regulations for prison management.

127.s:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I : In India, prisons are managed by State Governments with their own rules and regulations for the dayto-day administration of prisons.
Statement-II : In India, prisons are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 which expressly kept the subject of prisons in the control of Provincial Governments. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
127.x: As per the provisions of the Constitution of India, ‘prisons’/ ‘persons detained therein’ is a ‘State’ subject under entry 4 of the State List. In India, prisons are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 which vested the Provincial Governments (now States) with the power to make rules on prisons so the responsibility of prisons management and prisoners’administration solely vests with State Governments who alone are competent to make appropriate legislative provisions in this regard. However, given the critical role that efficient prison management plays in the criminal justice system, recently, the Ministry of Home Affairs has finalised a comprehensive ‘Model Prisons Act, 2023’, which may serve as a guiding document for the States, and for adoption in their jurisdiction. Hence statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 2 is the correct explanation of statement 1.

127.s: According to a survey conducted by London based Human Rights Organization, which one of the following countries is the world’s biggest state executioner?
127.x: The London based International Human Rights Organization, 'Amnesty International' released a report on the current status of the death penalty around the world. According to this report, in 2017, a total of 23 countries executed death penalty. By the end of 2017, a total of 106 countries abolished the death penalty for all crimes through legislation. China has the highest number of death sentences in 2017. Second Most (507+) (estimated figure) were executed in Iran in the year

128.s:
Consider the following statements about women's studies and constitutional provisions:
1. Neera Desai founded the first Women's Studies Centre at SNDT.
2. Article 15(3) of the Constitution provides for special provisions for women and children.
3. Reservation of seats for women in Panchayats is provided under Article 243D.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Neera Desai founded the first Women's Studies Centre at SNDT.
Statement 2: Correct: Article 15(3) enables the State to make special provisions for women and children.
Statement 3: Correct: Article 243D covers Panchayats; 243T covers Municipalities.

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 243D — reservation of seats and chairperson offices in Panchayats
Article 42 — reservation of seats in State Assemblies
128.x: Article 243D provides for at least one-third reservation of seats and chairperson offices in Panchayats. Article 243T relates to Municipalities.
128.tq: Use the local-body distinction between Panchayats and Municipalities.
xs: **Art. 243D** reserves at least **one-third** seats and **chairpersons' offices** in **Panchayats** — option **(3)**.
**Art. 243T** is for **Municipalities**, not Panchayats; Art. 243D is not about Municipalities.
**Art. 42** is about **maternity relief**; Assembly seats are under **Art. 332A**.
xa: **AP** gives **50%** to women in panchayats and municipalities — above the **1/3** floor.
About **46%** of PRI representatives are women (**26 Jan 2026**).
**Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** trains women elected representatives.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about women's reservation:
1. Andhra Pradesh provides 50% reservation for women in panchayats and municipalities, above the one-third floor.
2. In Andhra Pradesh, women's horizontal reservation in direct recruitment is 33 1/3%.
3. The 33% women's quota under the 106th Constitutional Amendment came into effect on 17 April 2026 in the Legislative Assemblies of Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Andhra Pradesh provides 50% reservation for women in panchayats and municipalities, above the one-third floor.
Statement 2: Correct: the horizontal reservation is 33 1/3%; women get 50% of nominated posts and work contracts.
Statement 3: Correct: the quota came into effect in the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies on 17 April 2026.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about women's rights law and amendments:
1. India's reservation, as distinct from its declarations, under CEDAW relates to Article 29(1).
2. Challenges to the marital rape exception that have reached the Supreme Court concern Section 64 of the BNS.
3. The Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026 was ratified by half the States on 17 April 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Correct: India's reservation is on Article 29(1); Articles 5(a), 16(1) and 16(2) carry declarations.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the marital rape exception challenged in the Supreme Court is under BNS Section 63, not Section 64.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the Bill was defeated by the Opposition on 17 April 2026.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about women's succession and representation:
1. The Indian Succession Act was enacted in 1925.
2. Gender budgeting, equal opportunities, workplace safety and participation in decision-making are components of an environmental audit.
3. The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 reserves one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Indian Succession Act came in 1925, the Hindu Succession Act in 1956.
Statement 2: Incorrect: all four are components of a gender audit, not an environmental audit.
Statement 3: Correct: the 106th Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) reserves one-third of seats for women.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about women's rights laws and schemes:
1. The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 is also known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.
2. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was first launched in 2014.
3. The Dowry Prohibition Act bans prenatal sex determination to stop female feticide.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the 106th Amendment Act, 2023 is the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, reserving one-third of seats for women.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao began in 2015, not 2014.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the PCPNDT Act, not the Dowry Prohibition Act, bans sex determination.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about laws and milestones for women:
1. The Devadasi system was prohibited in Andhra Pradesh by the Madras Act, 1947 only.
2. The Child Marriage Restraint Act, commonly known as the Sarda Act, was enacted in 1929.
3. The UN Decade for Women covered the period 1976–1985.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: it was banned by the Madras Act, 1947 and also by the AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988.
Statement 2: Correct: the Sarda Act was enacted in 1929 and dealt with the minimum marriage age.
Statement 3: Correct: the UN Decade for Women extended from 1976 to 1985.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Acts protecting women:
1. The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act, which bans sati and its glorification, was enacted in 1987.
2. The Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act was enacted in 1986.
3. The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 deals only with child marriage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Act was enacted in 1987.
Statement 2: Correct: it came in 1986, after the Dowry Prohibition Act (1961) and before the Sati Act (1987).
Statement 3: Incorrect: the ITPA penalises brothel-keeping, soliciting and living on the earnings of prostitution, and has nothing to do with child marriage.

128.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 — Decision within 60 days
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 — Internal Complaints Committee at the workplace
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 — Right to Residence under Section 17
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 — Right to Residence under Section 17
128.x: Right to Residence under Section 17 belongs to the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. The 2013 workplace law provides for an Internal Complaints Committee and a Local Complaints Committee in the district.
128.tq: Distinguish provisions of two neighbouring women-protection laws rather than matching only their subject.
xs: **Workplace Act 2013 — Right to Residence (Sec. 17)** is wrongly matched — option **(3)**.
**Right to Residence (Sec. 17)** and decision within **60 days** belong to the **Domestic Violence Act 2005**.
The **2013 Act** provides an **Internal Complaints Committee** at the workplace.
xa: The 2013 Act also has a **Local Complaints Committee** in the district.
The **DV Act 2005** is a **civil law**.
Crimes against women: **4,41,534** in **2024**; **32%** spousal violence (NFHS-5).

128.s: Which of the following pairs (law — year) is correctly matched?
o: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act — 1994
128.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act dates to 1961; ITPA is 1956, PCPNDT 1994 and the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act 2019.
xa: The **2019** Act was Parliament's response to **Shayara Bano**, passed **30 July 2019**.
**PCPNDT** bans sex selection and pre-natal sex determination.
Dowry: minimum **5 years** + fine of at least **Rs 15,000**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about personal and labour laws for women:
1. The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for monogamy and grounds of divorce under Hindu personal law.
2. The MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021 prohibits disclosure of the woman's identity.
3. The Code on Wages, 2019 subsumes the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for monogamy and specifies grounds of divorce.
Statement 2: Correct: the Act prohibits disclosure of the woman's identity, so it may not be disclosed without restriction.
Statement 3: Correct: the Code subsumes the Equal Remuneration Act along with the Minimum Wages, Payment of Wages and Payment of Bonus Acts.

128.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched under the ART (Regulation) Act, 2021?
o: National registry — Regulatory record of ART institutions
Sale of gametes or embryos — Prohibited
128.x: Sex-selective ART is prohibited under the ART Act, 2021. Registered clinics and banks and a national registry are permitted regulatory arrangements.
128.tq: Locate the option that reverses a statutory prohibition.
xs: **Sex-selective ART — Permitted** is wrong — option **(2)**: the **ART Act 2021** **prohibits** it.
**Registered ART clinics and banks** and a **national registry** are permitted; **sale of gametes/embryos** is prohibited.
xa: **PCPNDT Act 1994** bans sex selection and pre-natal sex determination.
The **Surrogacy Act 2021** also prohibits **sex selection**.
Commercial surrogacy is banned.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about labour codes and maternity benefit:
1. The Minimum Wages Act, 1948 was not absorbed into the Code on Wages, 2019.
2. Under the OSH Code, 2020, women may work before 6 a.m. or after 7 p.m. when they consent and prescribed safety safeguards are provided.
3. The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 provides for paid maternity leave of 12 weeks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Code absorbed the Minimum Wages Act; the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 was the one not absorbed.
Statement 2: Correct: the OSH Code permits such work with the women's consent and subject to safety safeguards.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the 2017 amendment raised paid maternity leave from 12 to 26 weeks for women with fewer than two surviving children.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about maternity benefit law:
1. Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, paid maternity leave was 16 weeks for establishments with 50 or more employees.
2. Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, the maternity benefit for the third child onwards is 12 weeks.
3. A woman adopting a child below three months of age is entitled under the 2017 amendment to maternity benefit for eight weeks before the adoption and four weeks after it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the 1961 Act provided 12 weeks of paid leave and applied to establishments employing 10 or more persons.
Statement 2: Correct: the third child onwards gets 12 weeks; the longer period applies to the first two children.
Statement 3: Incorrect: an adopting mother is entitled to 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over to her.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about women's welfare laws and sex ratio:
1. A crèche facility is mandatory under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 in an establishment having 100 or more employees, with one visit a day.
2. Female foeticide and infanticide is not a stated cause of a low sex ratio.
3. The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 declares instant Talaq-e-Biddat void and illegal, with imprisonment up to three years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: a crèche is required in establishments with 50 or more employees, with four visits a day.
Statement 2: Incorrect: female foeticide or infanticide is a stated cause; equal inheritance and universal schooling are not.
Statement 3: Correct: the 2019 Act makes instant talaq-e-biddat void, illegal and punishable with up to three years in prison.

128.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 provides inheritance rights to Hindus.
The Indian Succession Act, 1925 applies mainly to Muslims and others.
Muslim inheritance is governed by Sharia principles under Muslim Personal Law.
The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 granted daughters equal coparcenary rights.
128.x: Option B is incorrect: the Indian Succession Act, 1925 applies mainly to Christians and others. Muslims follow Sharia under their personal law.
128.tq: Match each community to its inheritance law.
n: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956, provides inheritance rights to Hindus. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 54-56]
The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, granted daughters equal coparcenary rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 54-56]
The Indian Succession Act, 1925, applies mainly to Christians and others. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 54-56]
Muslim inheritance is governed by Sharia principles. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 54-56]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the **Indian Succession Act, 1925** applies mainly to **Muslims** — option **(2)**; it applies mainly to **Christians and others**.
**Muslim inheritance** is governed by **Sharia principles**.
The **Hindu Succession Act, 1956** gives Hindus inheritance rights; the **2005 amendment** gave daughters **equal coparcenary rights**.
xa: HSA 1956 **abolished the female heir's limited estate**.
**AP** made unmarried daughters coparceners in **1986** — well before 2005 (Assembly passed it on **24 Sept 1985** under **NTR**).
HSA does **not apply to notified STs** (**s.2(2)**).

128.s:
Consider the following statements about marriage and workplace laws:
1. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides a civil, secular framework for marriage irrespective of caste, religion or faith, after public notice.
2. Under the POSH Act, 2013, Internal Complaints Committees are mandated in workplaces having at least 10 employees.
3. The PCPNDT Act, 1994 permits sex determination in ultrasound clinics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides civil, secular marriage for anyone after a public notice.
Statement 2: Correct: the POSH Act requires an Internal Complaints Committee in every workplace with 10 or more employees.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the PCPNDT Act bans sex determination.

128.s: Which of the following pairs (Act — year) is correctly matched?
128.x: The MTP Act dates from 1971; the Special Marriage Act is 1954, the Hindu Marriage Act 1955 and the Dowry Prohibition Act 1961.
n: The Special Marriage Act was enacted in 1954. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in 1955. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Dowry Prohibition Act was enacted in 1961. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act was enacted in 1971. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
xa: Dowry Act came into force on **July 1, 1961**; MTP Act on **April 1, 1972**.
**Maternity Benefit Act** is also of **1961**.
MTP amended on **September 24, 2021**.

128.s: Which of the following law–provision pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Hindu Marriage Act – Conditions of marriage, divorce and restitution of conjugal rights
Hindu Succession Act – Equal coparcenary rights to daughters by birth
POSH Act – Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with 10 or more employees
Prohibition of Child Marriage Act – Equal coparcenary rights to daughters
128.x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act makes child marriages voidable; coparcenary rights come under the Hindu Succession law.
n: The Hindu Marriage Act codified conditions of Hindu marriage, divorce, and restitution of conjugal rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]

n: The Bengal Sati Regulation was enacted in 1829. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Bengal Sati Regulation abolished Sati. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]

128.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Special Marriage Act commenced on January 1, 1955.
The PCPNDT Act commenced on January 1, 1994.

128.x: Option B is incorrect: the PCPNDT Act was passed in 1994 but came into force on 1 January 1996. The trap mixes up the year it was passed with the year it took effect.

n: The Special Marriage Act came into force on January 1, 1955. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Dowry Prohibition Act came into force on July 1, 1961. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]

xs: The incorrect statement is that **PCPNDT** commenced on **January 1, 1994** — option **(2)**; it was passed in **1994** and came into force on **January 1, 1996**.

xa: **Hindu Marriage Act** came into force **May 18, 1955**.

**POSH Act** came into force **December 9, 2013**.

128.s:

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

Its enactment year does not explain the commencement date.

128.s:
1. The National Commission for Women was established in 1992.
2. The first Equal Pay law was enacted in 1976.
3. The National Mission for Empowerment of Women was launched in 2015.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?

n: The first National Commission for Women was established in 1992. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Maternity Benefit Act was the first Maternity Benefit Law in 1961. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Equal Remuneration Act was the first Equal Pay Law in 1976. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The first National Mission for Women Empowerment was launched in 2010. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao programme was first launched in 2015. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]

xs: Both A and R are true, but **R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
The **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act** was enacted in **2006** — true.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about women's rights laws and cases:
1. The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 is associated with civil marriage irrespective of religion.
2. Saroj Rani v. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha recognised daughters' coparcenary rights by birth.
3. Gender mainstreaming aims to reduce gender discrimination, ensure equitable development and promote inclusive governance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the 2019 Act made instant triple talaq a crime; civil marriage is the Special Marriage Act.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Vineeta Sharma (2020) recognised daughters' coparcenary rights; Saroj Rani (1984) upheld restitution of conjugal rights.
Statement 3: Correct: reducing discrimination, equitable development and inclusive governance are all aims of gender mainstreaming.

128.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Child marriage — Marriage below the legally prescribed age
Devadasi — Dedication of girls to temples
128.x: Niyoga did not mean prohibition of widow remarriage; it involved a childless widow or wife bearing a son by the husband’s brother or kinsman.
128.tq: Find the wrong definition among closely related social customs.
xs: **Niyoga — Prohibition of widow remarriage** is wrongly matched — option **(2)**.
**Niyoga** = a **childless widow/wife bearing a son** by the husband's **brother or kinsman**.
**Devadasi** = girls dedicated to temples; **Sati** = widow immolation — both correctly matched.
xa: Devadasi was banned by the **Madras Act 1947** and the **AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act 1988**.
**Sati** was abolished in **1829** (Raja Rammohan Roy); the **Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act** is of **1987**.
**Vidyasagar**: **Widow Remarriage Act 1856**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian women's movement:
1. The Arya Mahila Samaj was founded by Pandita Ramabai.
2. Kandukuri Veeresalingam performed the first widow remarriage in Telugu society at Rajahmundry in 1881.
3. In the early 20th century, the focus of the Indian women's movement shifted to political rights.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj; the Phules founded the Satyashodhak Samaj.
Statement 2: Correct: Veeresalingam performed the first Telugu widow remarriage at Rajahmundry in 1881.
Statement 3: Correct: the 19th-century phase took up sati, widow remarriage and education; the early 20th century shifted to political rights.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about women's organisations and movements:
1. The Women's Indian Association (1917) was founded by Annie Besant and Pandita Ramabai.
2. The Anti-Arrack Movement in Andhra Pradesh began at Dubagunta in 1992.
3. Durgabai Deshmukh, founder of the Andhra Mahila Sabha, was also the first chairperson of the National Commission for Women (1992).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Annie Besant and Margaret Cousins founded the WIA.
Statement 2: Correct: it began at Dubagunta in 1992, leading to the arrack ban in 1993 and total prohibition in 1995.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Durgabai Deshmukh was the first chair of the Central Social Welfare Board (1953), not the NCW.

128.s:

Statement 1: Correct: the Gospel is by Mahendranath Gupta ('M'); Ram Mohan Roy wrote 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin'.
Statement 2: Correct: Savitribai Phule taught at the girls' school she and Jyotirao Phule opened in Pune in 1848.
Statement 3: Correct: the Widow Remarriage Act came in 1856, linked to Vidyasagar's movement.

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

n: The High-Caste Hindu Woman was written by Pandita Ramabai. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 13-15]
The High-Caste Hindu Woman concerns widow issues. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 13-15]

128.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Hindu Marriage Act
B. Bengal Sati Regulation
C. Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act
D. Child Marriage Restraint Act
128.x: The order is the Bengal Sati Regulation (1829), the Widow Remarriage Act (1856), the Child Marriage Restraint Act (1929) and the Hindu Marriage Act (1955), so the answer is B, C, D, A.
128.tq: Arrange the reform laws in time order.
n: The Bengal Sati Regulation was the first law against Sati in 1829. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Bengal Sati Regulation was the first law abolishing Sati in 1829. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The first Widow Remarriage Act was enacted in 1856. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act was the first Widow Remarriage Act in 1856. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Sharda Act was the first Child Marriage Restraint Law in 1929. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Child Marriage Restraint Act, also called the Sharda Act, was the first comprehensive child marriage law in 1929. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Hindu Marriage Act was the first codified Hindu Marriage Law after Independence in 1955. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xs: The order is **B, C, D, A** — option **(1)**.
**Bengal Sati Regulation** (**1829**) → **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act** (**1856**).
→ **Child Marriage Restraint (Sarda) Act** (**1929**) → **Hindu Marriage Act** (**1955**).
xa: The Sarda Act was replaced by the **PCMA, 2006**.
**Brahmo Samaj** was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in **1828**.
**Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** championed the **1856** Act.

128.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kandukuri Veeresalingam — Women's personal and sexual freedom through the novel Stree
Raja Rammohan Roy — Abolition of Sati
Pandita Ramabai — The High-Caste Hindu Woman
128.x: The statement is not correctly matched. Stree was written by Chalam, while Kandukuri Veeresalingam promoted widow remarriage and women's education in Telugu society.

xs: **Kandukuri Veeresalingam — Stree** is wrongly matched — option **(2)**: **Stree** is by **Chalam (Gudipati Venkata Chalam)**.
Veeresalingam brought **widow remarriage** and **women's education** to Telugu society.
The rest are correct: **Tarabai Shinde** – Stri Purush Tulana; **Rammohan Roy** – Sati abolition; **Pandita Ramabai** – The High-Caste Hindu Woman.
xa: Chalam wrote for women's **personal and sexual freedom**.
Veeresalingam's first Telugu widow remarriage: **1881, Rajahmundry**.
**Durgabai Deshmukh** founded the **Andhra Mahila Sabha (1937)**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about women's status and court rulings:
1. Vina Mazumdar was the Member-Secretary of the Committee on the Status of Women in India, which produced 'Towards Equality'.
2. The Haji Ali Dargah case decided by the Bombay High Court in 2016 concerned women's exclusion from the inner sanctum.
3. In Rakhi Bisht v. Union of India, the Delhi High Court held that maternity protection covers only promotion, but not status or posting.

Statement 1: Correct: Vina Mazumdar was Member-Secretary; the report exposed the declining status of women.
Statement 2: Correct: the case concerned the bar on women entering the inner sanctum; entry was ultimately allowed.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the court held that maternity protection extends to post, status and promotion.

128.s:
With reference to gender auditing:

2. It covers policies, programmes, institutions and budgets.
3. It is restricted to budgets alone.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is false because a gender audit covers policies, programmes and institutions as well as budgets.
xa: It **identifies gender gaps** and **improves women's participation**.
**Gender budgeting** is only one of its components.

128.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Committee on Status of Women in India was constituted in 1971 under the chairpersonship of Phulrenu Guha.
The High-Level Committee on Status of Women was constituted in 2012 under Pam Rajput.

128.tq: Discriminate the year a body was set up from its report year.
n: The Committee on the Status of Women in India was established in 1971. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
Phulrenu Guha chaired the Committee on the Status of Women in India. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Towards Equality Report was published in 1974. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]

128.s:
1. J.S. Verma chaired the Justice Verma Committee.
2. The High-Level Committee on the Status of Women worked on women's empowerment.

n: J. S. Verma chaired the Justice Verma Committee. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The purpose of the High-Level Committee on the Status of Women was women empowerment. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
