135.s: President Ram nath Kovind granted assent to which Constitutional Amendment Act on 18th August, 2021?
135.x: President Ram Nath Kovind granted assent to the 105th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2021 on 18th August, 2021. It empowers states to identify and specify the Socially and Educationally Backward Class (SEBC). As per the Act, every State or Union territory may, by law, prepare and maintain, for its own purposes, a list of socially and educationally backward classes, entries in which may be different from the Central List.

135.s:
Consider the following statements about reservation-related constitutional amendments:
1. Before the 102nd Constitutional Amendment, Article 338(10) provided that references to Scheduled Castes would include such backward classes as were specified by the President.
2. Article 15(5) was inserted by the 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act.
3. The 76th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1994 placed Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
135.x:
Statement 1: Correct: before the 102nd Amendment, Article 338(10) treated references to SCs as including backward classes specified by the President.
Statement 2: Correct: the 93rd Amendment (2005) inserted Article 15(5), enabling reservation in educational institutions including private unaided ones.
Statement 3: Correct: the 76th Amendment (1994) placed Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule.

135.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the ruling in Indra Sawhney regarding carry-forward vacancies?
o: Carry-forward is allowed, but it must operate within the 50 per cent ceiling on a year-by-year basis.
Carry-forward is prohibited in every situation.
Carry-forward applies only to EWS vacancies.
Carry-forward is unlimited and is calculated only once in a decade.
135.x: Indra Sawhney permitted carry-forward of vacancies, subject to the 50 per cent ceiling being applied year by year.
135.tq: Combine the carry-forward rule with the year-by-year ceiling rather than treating either as absolute.
xs: **Carry-forward** is allowed but must stay **within the 50% ceiling**, applied **year by year** — option **(1)**.
Indra Sawhney fixed total reservation **not above 50%** except in extraordinary cases.
It is not limited to EWS; EWS (**103rd**) came much later.
xa: The **81st (2000)** made unfilled **backlog vacancies** a separate class, outside the **50%** ceiling (**Art. 16(4B)**).
**Janhit Abhiyan**: the **50% cap** applies to backward-class quotas.
The **76th (1994)** put Tamil Nadu's **69%** law in the **Ninth Schedule**.

135.s: Which amendment-clause pair is correctly matched?
135.x: The First Amendment, 1951 inserted Article 15(4). Article 16(4A) was inserted by the 77th Amendment, Article 16(4B) by the 81st, Article 15(5) by the 93rd and Article 16(6) by the 103rd Amendment.
135.tq: Start with the sure amendment-clause pair and eliminate the swapped clauses.
xs: **First Amendment — Article 15(4)** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Art. 15(4)** was added to overcome **Champakam Dorairajan**.
xa: **81st (2000)** = **Art. 16(4B)** backlog vacancies.
**85th (2001)** = **consequential seniority**, nullifying the "catch-up" rule.

135.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The 82nd Amendment concerns relaxation of qualifying standards in promotion for SCs and STs.
The 81st Amendment deals with unfilled backlog vacancies.
The 89th Amendment introduced the relaxation of qualifying marks under Article 335.
The 77th Amendment deals with reservation in promotion for SCs and STs.
135.x: The 89th Amendment did not introduce the relaxation of qualifying marks; that change was made by the 82nd Amendment Act, 2000. The 89th Amendment is associated with the bifurcation of the SC/ST Commission.
135.tq: Find the wrong amendment-provision association among closely related reservation amendments.
xs: The NOT-correct statement is that the **89th Amendment introduced relaxation of qualifying marks** — option **(3)**.
Relaxation (proviso to **Art. 335**) came by the **82nd (2000)**; the **89th** split the **SC/ST Commission**.
Other statements are correct: **81st** = backlog vacancies; **77th** = promotion reservation for SCs/STs.
xa: ⚠ APPSC G2 **2024** keyed relaxation to the "**89th**" — WRONG.
**85th (2001)**: consequential seniority.
**76th (1994)**: TN **69%** law in the **Ninth Schedule**.

o: 77th Amendment – Reservation in promotion under Article 16(4A)
81st Amendment – Backlog vacancies as a separate class
135.x: The 82nd Amendment inserted the proviso to Article 335 on relaxing qualifying marks; consequential seniority came with the 85th.
xa: The **85th (2001)** nullified the "**catch-up**" rule.
**77th (1995)** answered **Indra Sawhney**.
**81st**: backlog vacancies sit outside the **50%** ceiling.

135.s:
Consider the following statements about reservation-related constitutional amendments:
1. The 93rd Constitutional Amendment (2005), which inserted Article 15(5), was enacted to overcome the P.A. Inamdar (2005) judgment.
2. The Union Government opposed applying the creamy-layer principle to SCs and STs on the ground that their status flows from Articles 341 and 342.
3. The 102nd Constitutional Amendment restored State power over SEBC lists, while the 105th created the NCBC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
135.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Article 15(5) was inserted to overcome P.A. Inamdar (2005), which had barred quotas in private unaided institutions.
Statement 2: Correct: in August 2026, the Union Government stated that SC/ST status flows from Articles 341 and 342.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the 102nd Amendment gave constitutional status to the NCBC and inserted Article 342A, while the 105th restored States' power to list SEBCs.

135.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indra Sawhney judgment:
1. According to the Indra Sawhney judgment, the backward classes referred to in Article 16(4) are to be identified mainly on the basis of place of residence.
2. The Indra Sawhney judgment did not extend OBC reservation to promotions as a general rule.
3. All children of persons belonging to OBC communities, irrespective of social or economic status, are not included among the OBC creamy-layer categories under the Indra Sawhney framework.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
135.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Indra Sawhney held that backward classes are identified mainly by caste and social backwardness, not place of residence.
Statement 2: Correct: Indra Sawhney confined reservation to initial appointments, not promotions.
Statement 3: Correct: the framework identifies specified socially advanced categories, such as children of Class-I officers, not all OBC children.

135.s:
Consider the following statements about backward-class reservation:
1. In the Sukhdev case on backward-class reservation in Andhra Pradesh, it was held that caste alone could not be the basis, and 112 classes were identified using poverty, residence and occupation.
2. The B.P. Mandal Commission was not constituted by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
3. The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, providing 27 per cent OBC reservation, came into force in 2007.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
135.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the High Court held that caste alone could not be the basis; 112 classes were listed using poverty, residence and occupation.
Statement 2: Correct: the Mandal Commission was set up through the Ministry of Home Affairs, not Social Justice and Empowerment.
Statement 3: Correct: although enacted in 2006, the Act came into force in 2007.

135.s:

2. The income ceiling for determining the OBC creamy layer, after the 2017 revision and still current, is ₹8 lakh per annum.
3. The Centre did not approve the 2017 BC-F proposal for Kapu reservation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
135.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the criteria were framed through the September 1993 DoPT Office Memorandum, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee.
Statement 2: Correct: the ceiling was revised to ₹8 lakh per annum in 2017 and is stated to remain current.
Statement 3: Correct: the Centre never approved the 2017 BC-F proposal.

135.s:
Consider the following statements about creamy layer and EWS reservation:
1. In Union of India v. Rohith Nathan, the Court did not hold that parental salary alone determines creamy-layer status.
2. The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act was introduced in Parliament as the 124th Amendment Bill.
3. For the States, EWS reservation under the 103rd Constitutional Amendment is enabling, not mandatory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
135.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Court held that parental salary alone cannot place a candidate in the creamy layer.
Statement 2: Correct: it originated as the 124th Amendment Bill and inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) for 10% EWS reservation.
Statement 3: Correct: the amendment enables up to 10% EWS reservation but does not make it mandatory for States.

135.s:
Consider the following statements about EWS reservation:
1. EWS reservation under the 103rd Amendment is not compulsory for State Governments.
2. The EWS eligibility criteria are annual family income below ₹10 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,500 sq ft.
3. In Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India, the 103rd Constitutional Amendment was upheld by a majority of 4:1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
135.x:
Statement 1: Correct: implementation of EWS reservation is not mandatory for State Governments.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the criteria are annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,000 sq ft.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the amendment was upheld 3:2, with Chief Justice U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat dissenting.

135.s:
Assertion (A): BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh local bodies was reduced to 24.15 per cent under GOs 176, 559 and 560.
Reason (R): N.T. Rama Rao introduced a 20 per cent BC quota in local bodies in 1984.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
135.x: Both are correct, but the 1984 introduction of the quota does not explain its later reduction from 34 to 24.15 per cent.
xa: The earlier **34%** was struck down for breaching the overall ceiling.
Current: **34% rural** + **33.33% urban** (19 Aug 2026).
**G.O. Rt. No. 1065** governs ULB polls.

135.s:
Consider the following statements about backward-class reservation:
1. The BC-E category in Andhra Pradesh was added through the 2007 Andhra Pradesh Act.
2. The Anantharaman Commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission and framed the A-D grouping along with a 25 per cent quota.
3. Article 15(4) was added to the Constitution to overcome the judgment in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
135.x:
Statement 1: Correct: BC-E was added by the Andhra Pradesh Act of 2007; earlier lists had only BC-A to BC-D.
Statement 2: Correct: the Anantharaman Commission, reporting in 1970, framed the A-D grouping and a 25 per cent quota.
Statement 3: Correct: Article 15(4) was inserted by the First Amendment, 1951 to overcome Champakam Dorairajan.

135.s:
The Supreme Court’s triple test for OBC reservation in local bodies requires:
1. A dedicated commission to examine backwardness.
2. Determination of the reservation proportion local-body-wise.
3. Keeping the total reservation within the 50 per cent ceiling.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: All three requirements form the triple test: a dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportional determination, and compliance with the overall 50 per cent ceiling.
135.tq: Recognise a judicial test as a cumulative set of mandatory conditions.
xs: All three are part of the **triple test** — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Dedicated commission** + **local-body-wise proportion** + total **within 50%**.
xa: AP's earlier **34%** was struck down for breaching the overall ceiling.
Current AP: **34% rural**, **33.33% urban**.
**Indra Sawhney**: **50%** ceiling except in extraordinary cases.

135.s: Which of the following statements about the expression “Backward Classes” in the Constitution is correct?
o: It is exhaustively defined in Article 15.
It is defined in Article 340 itself.
It is defined only in the Fifth Schedule.
It is not defined in the Constitution.
135.x: The Constitution does not define the expression “Backward Classes”; constitutional provisions instead provide mechanisms concerning their identification and welfare.
135.tq: Test the exact constitutional status of a frequently misattributed definition.
xs: "**Backward Classes**" is **not defined in the Constitution** — option **(4)**.
APPSC G2 **2017** key: the statement saying it is "defined" was the wrong one.
**Art. 340** only lets the **President** appoint a commission to investigate their conditions — it does not define the term.
xa: Under **Indra Sawhney**, **Art. 16(4)** backward classes are identified mainly by **caste/social backwardness**.
Correct term = **Socially and Educationally** Backward Classes (SEBCs).
For the **CEI Act**, OBCs are classes "so determined by the **Central Government**".
**Art. 366(26C)** defines SEBCs by reference to **Art. 342A**.

135.s: Which expression correctly expands SEBC in the context of Articles 342A and the 105th Amendment?
135.x: SEBC means Socially and Educationally Backward Classes. The expression 'Socially and Economically Backward Classes' is not the constitutional expansion used here.
135.tq: Test the exact official phrase rather than a familiar but altered expansion.
xs: SEBC = **Socially and Educationally Backward Classes** — option **(1)**.
⚠ IYB's "**Socially and Economically**" is WRONG.
xa: **Art. 366(26C)** defines SEBCs by reference to **Art. 342A**.
**105th (2021)** restored **States' power** to list SEBCs.
**Art. 15(5)** covers **SEBCs, SCs, STs** in admissions.

135.s: All following statements regarding Backward Classes are correct, except?
o: The word ' Backward Classes of Citizens ' is defined in the Constitution
The Backward Classes contemplated under Art 16 (4) are mainly social. It need not be both social and educational
By clause (10) of the Article 338 " Backward Classes " are included within expression " Scheduled Caste "
Indra Sawhney case is related to " Backward Classes "

135.s: Which one of the following has a status different from the other three?
135.x: The National Human Rights Commission is a non- Constitutional body, while the other three (Appointment of a commission to investigate the condition of Backward Classes - Article 340, National Commission for Backward Classes- Article 338 B, Finance Commission- Article 280 and Election Commission- Article 324) are the Constitutional bodies. 77. Which among the following is NOT correctly matched? Bodies Establishment (a) Inter-state Council - 1990 (b) National Development - 1954 Council (c) Central Vigilance - 1964 Commission (d) National Human Rights - 1993 Commission U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Mains) 2016 Ans. (b) The correctly matched order is as follows : Bodies Establishment (a) Inter-state Council - 1990 (b) National Development - 1952 Council (c) Central Vigilance - 1964 Commission (d) National Human Rights - 1993 Commission

135.s: By which Constitutional Amendment OBCs have been given 27 percent reservation in the admission to educational institutions?
135.x: The 93rd Amendment Act (passed in 2006) provided OBCs with 27% reservation in admission to educational institutions.

135.s: Mandal Commission, whose proposals created massive dispute, was set up by-
135.x: The Mandal Commission was constituted in India in 1979 by the Janata Party Government under former Prime Minister Morarji Desai with a mandate to “identify the socially and educationally backward persons.” It was headed by an Indian Parliamentarian, Bindheshwari Prasad Mandal.

135.s: The Report of Mandal Commission was submitted in-
135.x: In 1979, the Janta Party Government constituted the Mandal Commission presided over by Bindheshwari Prasad Mandal (B.P. Mandal). The Commission submitted its report in 1980.

135.s: Which of the following Constitutional Amendments provided rights for making provisions in favour of the SCs and STs for relaxation of qualifying marks in any examination (or) lowering the standards of evaluation and for reservation in the matter of promotions to the public services of the Centre 89. As and the State?
Under which Amendment Act was the reservation in promotion for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes ensured by inserting Clause '4A' in Article 16?
135.x: The 77th Amendment Act, 1995 ensured the reservation in promotion for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes by inserting clause (4A) in the Article- 16.

135.s: Which one of the following States has proposed reservation for Muslims in jobs and education ?
135.x: The government of Andhra Pradesh provided reservations to Muslims for jobs and education in 2004 this was cancelled by the Andhra Pradesh High Court. Later in 2007, the Government of Andhra Pradesh limited the reservation for Muslims to 4 per cent in accordance with 50% limit, but it was again cancelled by the High Court. Nevertheless, the Supreme Court', through its interim decision', accepted the reservation made by the Andhra Pradesh Government. But the final decision is still awaited as the matter is pending before the Constitutional Bench of the Supreme Court.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about tribal rights and movements:
1. In tribal usage, the term 'Diku' refers to an outsider-exploiter such as a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor.
2. The Forest Conservation Rules, 2022 became a subject of dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry because they prohibited all development projects in forest areas.
3. T. K. Oommen identified political autonomy, recognition of identity and control over resources as objectives of modern tribal movements.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Diku denotes an outsider-exploiter, including a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the dispute arose because the 2022 Rules dropped the forest-dwellers' consent clause before forest diversion.
Statement 3: Correct: T. K. Oommen identified political autonomy, identity recognition and control over resources as these objectives.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about tribal development policy:
1. The first principle of Nehru's Panchsheel for tribal development is to impose a uniform administration on all tribal areas.
2. That tribal people should be relied upon and trained for their own administration is not a Panchsheel principle for tribal development.
3. The NSTFDC does not lend to STs with income up to three times the poverty line.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the first principle is to develop tribal people along the lines of their own genius.
Statement 2: Incorrect: it is a Panchsheel principle; the one that is not is judging results by money spent rather than by the quality of human character evolved.
Statement 3: Correct: NSTFDC lends to STs with income up to double, not three times, the poverty line.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about tribal welfare institutions:
1. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was set up as a separate Union Ministry in 1999.
2. The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A was created by the 91st Amendment, 2003.
3. Raising farm output with improved seeds and fertilisers, planting fruit-bearing trees and other income-raising activities in tribal areas are objectives of TADP/ITDA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Ministry of Tribal Affairs was set up in 1999.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Article 338A was inserted by the 89th Amendment, 2003, not the 91st.
Statement 3: Correct: these are objectives of TADP/ITDA.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about tribal and SC welfare administration:
1. Monitoring of the Tribal Sub-Plan moved from the Planning Commission to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in January 2017.
2. PM-AJAY, launched in 2021-22, is administered as a centrally sponsored intervention by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
3. The nodal Ministry for implementation of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 is the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Correct: TSP monitoring shifted to MoTA in January 2017.
Statement 2: Correct: PM-AJAY was launched in 2021-22 as a 100 per cent centrally funded scheme under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, not Environment, is the nodal ministry for the Forest Rights Act, 2006.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about the Forest Rights Act, 2006:
1. Claims under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 are not examined by Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees.
2. Automatic ownership of all mineral resources beneath forest land is not recognised as a forest right under the Forest Rights Act, 2006.
3. The Forest Rights Act, 2006 sought to undo the historical injustice done to forest dwellers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: claims are examined by Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees, which are six-member bodies.
Statement 2: Correct: the Act recognises rights such as minor forest produce and community forest resources, not ownership of minerals.
Statement 3: Correct: the Act's stated objective is undoing historical injustice to forest dwellers.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about the Forest Rights Act, 2006:
1. Occupation of forest land before 13 December 2005 is the relevant date for a forest-dwelling ST family claiming rights under the Forest Rights Act.
2. For recognition under the Forest Rights Act, Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must establish residence in or dependence on forests for one generation or 25 years.
3. The maximum extent of forest rights that may be recognised per family under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 is 4 hectares.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Correct: forest-dwelling STs must have occupied the forest land before 13 December 2005.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show three generations, specified as 75 years.
Statement 3: Correct: the ceiling is up to four hectares per family.

136.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with an individual forest right rather than a community forest right?
136.x: Habitation and self-cultivation are individual rights. Nistar, grazing, fishing and community forest resource management are examples of community rights.
136.tq: Separate individual and community rights by identifying the beneficiary and nature of use.
xs: **Habitation and self-cultivation** are **individual** rights — option **(1)**.
**Grazing**, **fishing** and **CFR management** are **community** rights.
xa: Community rights also include **nistar**.
Other rights: **ownership of MFP**, **habitat rights for PVTGs**.
⚠ Implementation gap: focus on **individual titles over CFR**.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about the Forest Rights Act, 2006:
1. The Forest Rights Act, 2006 is subordinate to every earlier forest law.
2. The Baiga of Chhattisgarh was the first Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group stated to have received habitat rights under the Forest Rights Act framework.
3. Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, 'nistar' is classified as a community right.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Forest Rights Act overrides laws that are inconsistent with it.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the Bharia of Madhya Pradesh were the first; Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh followed.
Statement 3: Correct: nistar, grazing, fishing and minor forest produce rights are listed community rights under the FRA.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about forest rights and diversion:
1. Critical Wildlife Habitat under the Forest Rights Act refers to areas of national parks and sanctuaries that are to be opened for mining after approval by the Forest Department.
2. The Indian Forest (Amendment) Act, 2017 removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of "tree".
3. Forest diversion is not permissible before completion of FRA claims merely because the project is of public importance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Critical Wildlife Habitats are to be kept inviolate, notified after an open process with affected communities.
Statement 2: Correct: the 2017 amendment removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of "tree".
Statement 3: Correct: MoEFCC guidelines barred forest diversion until FRA processes, especially Gram Sabha consent, were complete, as upheld by the Supreme Court.

136.s: Which one of the following statements regarding bamboo under the Forest Rights Act is correct?
o: Bamboo is a tree in every location and cannot be collected by forest dwellers.
Bamboo is a minor forest produce, and ownership is vested in forest dwellers.
Bamboo is excluded from minor forest produce and belongs only to the Forest Department.
Ownership of bamboo is vested only in Gram Panchayats.
136.x: The Forest Rights Act treats bamboo as a minor forest produce and vests its ownership in forest dwellers.
136.tq: Separate the FRA status of bamboo from its treatment under the Indian Forest Act amendment.
xs: **Bamboo is a minor forest produce** under the FRA, with **ownership vested in forest dwellers** — option **(2)**.
UPSC **2019** key: this was the correct statement.
xa: **IFA (Amendment) 2017** removed bamboo grown **outside forest areas** from "tree".
⚠ IFA 2017 did **not** give a right to fell bamboo in forest areas.
**TRIFED** gives **MSP for MFP**.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about tribal land and forest rights:
1. Restrictive MFP transit permits are not a reported gap in Forest Rights Act implementation.
2. Under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, Social Impact Assessment is required only for private projects and never for public projects.
3. In Scheduled Areas, acquisition under the RFCTLARR Act is a last resort and requires consent of the Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: restrictive MFP transit permits are a reported gap; the item that is not is strong MoTA capacity, since the gap is weak capacity.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 makes Social Impact Assessment mandatory.
Statement 3: Correct: acquisition in Scheduled Areas is a last resort and requires consent of the Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council.

136.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: TRIFED — 1987 — tribal marketing and MSP for Minor Forest Produce
Roshni — 2018 — residential schools for SC students
VDVKs — 2013 — skills and jobs in LWE districts
PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission — 1987 — sanitation mechanisation
136.x: TRIFED was established in 1987 and is associated with tribal marketing and MSP for Minor Forest Produce. The other options interchange the purposes or years of different programmes.
136.tq: Start from the distinctive year-purpose pair and eliminate cross-matched programmes.
xs: **TRIFED — 1987 — tribal marketing and MSP for MFP** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Roshni** = skills and jobs for tribal youth in **LWE** districts (**MoRD, 2013**).
**VDVKs** = **2018**; **PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission** = **2021-22** (MFP at MSP, not sanitation).
xa: TRIFED brand: "**Tribes India**".
VDVKs: **4,172** nationally; AP **415** sanctioned.
Sanitation mechanisation = **NAMASTE**.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about tribal welfare schemes:
1. The PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission, run by TRIFED, includes buying MFP at MSP, value addition and GI tags.
2. Roshni is a programme for skills and jobs for tribal youth in Left-Wing Extremism districts.
3. Eklavya Model Residential Schools are a Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission, run by TRIFED, focuses on buying MFP at MSP, value addition and GI tags.
Statement 2: Correct: Roshni provides skills and employment for tribal youth in LWE districts.
Statement 3: Correct: EMRS is a Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about schemes for SCs and STs:
1. The cost of the SC Post-Matric Scholarship is not shared in the ratio 75:25.
2. Stand-Up India was not launched on 5 April 2016.
3. The Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence provide free Civil Services coaching to SC students in Central Universities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the SC Post-Matric Scholarship cost is shared 60:40, not 75:25.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the launch date of 5 April 2016 is correct; the incorrect claim is that Stand-Up India is meant exclusively for existing enterprises, when it supports greenfield ones.
Statement 3: Correct: the Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence give free Civil Services coaching to SC students in Central Universities.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about tribal welfare administration:
1. The Girijan Cooperative Corporation purchases minor forest produce at fair prices, runs PDS depots and gives credit to tribal farmers in Andhra Pradesh.
2. In August 2026, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change stated that the Forest Rights Act has no provision for Gram Sabha consent for Stage-II forest clearance.
3. The Ministry of Minority Affairs is the nodal ministry for the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the GCC purchases MFP at fair prices, runs PDS depots and provides credit to tribal farmers.
Statement 2: Incorrect: it was the Ministry of Tribal Affairs that made this statement in August 2026.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the Abhiyan is led by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, not Minority Affairs.

136.s:
Assertion (A): MoTA sought MoEFCC funds for managing Community Forest Resource areas vested in Gram Sabhas.
Reason (R): Eviction orders in Agasthyamalai were criticised for ignoring the Forest Rights Act.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
136.x: Both statements are true, but they are separate issues: the CFR funding request is not explained by the criticism of the Agasthyamalai eviction orders.
xa: STs about **9%** of population but **over 50%** of displaced.
**Forest Conservation Rules 2022** dropped prior consent.
Over **47,900** CFR/CFRR claims rejected.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about the Forest Rights Act, 2006:
1. It recognises individual and community forest rights.
2. These rights are recognised for forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
136.x: Both are correct: the Act recognises individual and community forest rights of forest-dwelling STs and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.
n: The Forest Rights Act was passed in 2006. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Forest Rights Act recognizes individual forest rights for forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Forest Rights Act recognizes community forest rights for forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Forest Rights Act recognizes individual forest rights for Other Traditional Forest Dwellers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Forest Rights Act recognizes community forest rights for Other Traditional Forest Dwellers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xa: The FRA aims to undo the **"historical injustice"** to forest dwellers; nodal ministry: **Tribal Affairs**.
FDST cut-off: occupying forest land **before 13 December 2005**.
OTFDs must show **3 generations (75 years)** of dependence.
Ceiling: up to **4 hectares per family**.

136.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Forest Rights Act is correctly matched?
o: Rights vested – Individual and community forest rights
136.x: The FRA was passed in 2006, came into force on 31 December 2007, had its rules notified on 1 January 2008, and vests individual and community forest rights.
n: The Forest Rights Act was enacted in 2006. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Forest Rights Act came into force on December 31, 2007. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The rules under the Forest Rights Act were notified on January 1, 2008. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Forest Rights Act vests individual forest rights in forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Forest Rights Act vests community forest rights in forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Forest Rights Act vests individual forest rights in Other Traditional Forest Dwellers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Forest Rights Act vests community forest rights in Other Traditional Forest Dwellers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
xa: **Sec. 6**: the **Gram Sabha** initiates determination of rights.
**Six-member** Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees examine claims.
Community rights include **nistar**, **grazing**, fishing and **CFR** management.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission:
1. It is associated with the Ministries of Health & Family Welfare and Tribal Affairs.
2. It focuses on screening tribal populations.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
136.x: Both are correct: the Mission is run by Health & Family Welfare with Tribal Affairs and focuses on screening tribal populations.
n: The nodal ministries for the National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission are the Ministries of Health and Family Welfare and Tribal Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
The National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission focuses heavily on screening tribal populations. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
The National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission is a key initiative for Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xa: Target: **elimination** of sickle cell anaemia by **2047**.
The **Sickle Cell Mission Portal** tracks **screening cards** in a **central registry**.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-AJAY:
1. Its portal supports planning and monitoring of works in SC-majority Adarsh Grams.
2. It includes fund convergence.
3. It is a portal for tribal artisans to sell forest produce.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
136.x: 1 and 2 are correct: PM-AJAY plans, pools funds for and monitors works in SC-majority Adarsh Grams. 3 is wrong; the tribal artisans' marketplace is TRIFED/Tribes India.
n: The PM-AJAY Portal is a digital platform for Scheduled Castes (SC). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-AJAY Portal supports end-to-end planning of infrastructure works. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-AJAY Portal supports fund convergence for infrastructure works. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-AJAY Portal monitors infrastructure works. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-AJAY Portal covers SC-majority Adarsh Gram infrastructure works. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TRIFED and Tribes India E-Marketplace are digital platforms for Scheduled Tribes (ST). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TRIFED and Tribes India E-Marketplace provide a dedicated e-commerce gateway. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TRIFED and Tribes India E-Marketplace connect tribal artisans directly to buyers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TRIFED and Tribes India E-Marketplace connect forest-produce collectors directly to buyers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
xa: PM-AJAY Portal is run by the **Department of Social Justice and Empowerment**.
TRIFED also offers **MSP for Minor Forest Produce**.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about Scheduled Tribes in India:
1. A community is included as a Scheduled Tribe through a State proposal, examination by the Registrar General of India and NCST, consideration by the Union Cabinet, and amendment of the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 by Parliament.
2. The term 'Scheduled Tribes' is defined in Article 342(2) of the Constitution of India.
3. The Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) scheme started in 1997-98.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Correct: this is the stated sequence, with Parliament amending the Order under Article 342(2).
Statement 2: Incorrect: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes; Article 342(2) lets Parliament modify the ST list.
Statement 3: Correct: EMRS began in 1997-98; its target is 740 schools and Odisha has the highest number.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about tribal land and resistance:
1. Colonial moneylenders and revenue farmers contributed to tribal indebtedness and land alienation during colonial rule.
2. Birsa Munda's Ulgulan was directed against the establishment of Eklavya schools.
3. In 2013, Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected the Niyamgiri bauxite mining under the FRA, and the project was cancelled.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Correct: colonial moneylenders and revenue farmers contributed to indebtedness and land alienation.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Birsa's Ulgulan was aimed at British land-grabbing and the exploitative dikus.
Statement 3: Correct: Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected the mining under the Forest Rights Act, and the project was cancelled.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about land and welfare laws:
1. Under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, the consent of 80% of affected families is required for private projects and 70% for public-private partnership projects.
2. The NAMASTE scheme is implemented by NSKFDC.
3. The Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation, 1959 primarily seeks to bar transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Correct: consent of 80% of affected families is required for private projects and 70% for PPP projects.
Statement 2: Correct: NAMASTE is implemented by NSKFDC; TRIFED is not its implementing agency.
Statement 3: Correct: Regulation 1 of 1959 bars the transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about tribal land laws in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The 1970 amendment to the Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation applied it only to urban municipal areas.
2. In Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997), the Supreme Court held that the AP land transfer regulation does not apply to mining leases.
3. G.O. No. 3 (2000), which gave 100% of Scheduled Area teacher posts to local STs, was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the 1970 amendment added a presumption that the land belongs to tribals and prohibited transfers even between non-tribals.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Samatha held that Scheduled Area land cannot be transferred or leased to non-tribals or private companies, including private mining companies.
Statement 3: Correct: G.O. No. 3 was issued in 2000 and struck down by the Supreme Court in 2020.

136.s:
Assertion (A): Private non-tribal mining companies may obtain mining leases in Scheduled Areas of Andhra Pradesh if the Gram Sabha gives consent.
Reason (R): The State is barred from leasing Scheduled Area land to non-tribals.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
136.x: The State is barred from leasing Scheduled Area land to non-tribals, so mining is left to State undertakings or tribal cooperatives; Gram Sabha consent does not validate a private non-tribal lease.
xa: Samatha (**1997**) arose from mining leases in the **Visakhapatnam Agency**.
AP: soil sampling for bauxite in **Chintapalli and G.K. Veedhi**.

136.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The definition of "Critical Wildlife Habitat is incorporated in the Forest Rights Act, of 2006.
2. For the first time in India, Baigas have been given Habitat Rights.
3. Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change officially decides and declares Habitat Rights for Primitive and Vulnerable Tribal Groups in any part of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x: Statement 1 is correct: The phrase 'critical wildlife habitat' is defined only in the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006. CWH are defined under the act as the "areas of national parks and sanctuaries where it has been specifically and clearly established, case by case, on the basis of scientific and objective criteria, that such areas are required to be kept as inviolate for the purposes of wildlife conservation". Inviolate is a general term used to indicate no human settlement or usage. Statement 2 is correct: The Baiga community in Madhya Pradesh became the first tribe in India to receive habitat rights under the Forest Rights Act of 2006. Statement 3 is incorrect: The process involves District Level Committee (DLC), Gram Sabha, State Government, and Ministry of Tribal Affairs, not MoEFCC. PMF Concept Hack: India has a dedicated Ministry of Tribal Affairs for tribal welfare, so it is highly unlikely that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change would independently decide and declare Habitat Rights for tribal groups. Hence, Statement 3 can be eliminated. Once Statement 3 is removed, options containing 3 are also eliminated, leaving Statements 1 and 2 as correct.

136.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. As per recent amendment to the Indian Forest Act, 1927, forest dwellers have the right to fell the bamboos grown on forest areas.
2. As per the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, bamboo is a minor forest produce.
3. The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 allows ownership of minor forest produce to forest dwellers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x: Statement 1 is incorrect: An amendment was made in 2017-18 in the Indian Forest Act of 1927 to remove bamboo from the category of trees. With this minor modification, bamboo grown in non-forest areas will not require a transit permit (TP) and other legal permits for felling and transportation from the forest department. However, bamboo grown in the forest would continue to require a TP and other legal permits. Statement 2 is correct: Minor Forest Produce (MFP) is a subset of forest produce and got a definition only in 2007 when the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, was enacted. Section 2(i) of the said Act defines a Minor Forest Produce (MFP) as all non-timber forest produce of plant origin and includes bamboo, brushwood, stumps, canes, Tusser, cocoon, honey, waxes, Lac, tendu/kendu leaves, medicinal plants and herbs, roots, tubers, and the like. Statement 3 is correct: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, popularly known as the Forest Rights Act (FRA), was enacted in 2007. The Act recognises and vests individual forest-dwellers with forest rights to live in and cultivate forest land that was occupied before 13 December 2005, and grants community forest rights to manage, protect, and regenerate the forest, and to own and dispose of minor forest products from forests where they had traditional access. Individuals, communities and gram sabhas have right

2. It rewrote Article 45 to address early childhood care up to six years.

1: UNCRC has **54 articles**. 2: India acceded in **1992** (**11 December**).
3 is wrong: India's Children's Day is **14 November**; Universal Children's Day is **20 November**.

Statement 3: Correct: the 86th Amendment (2002) made education a Fundamental Right.

137.s:
Which of the following are associated with monitoring and grievance redressal under the RTE Act?
1. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
2. State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights
3. School Management Committees as statutory child-rights commissions
137.x: NCPCR and SCPCRs monitor and redress grievances under the RTE Act; School Management Committees are school-level bodies, not statutory child-rights commissions.
xa: NCPCR set up in **2007** under the **CPCR Act 2005**.
**SC (Jan 2026)** directed **NCPCR** to monitor the RTE quota.
AP SCPCR member **V. Gandhi Babu** ordered admission of migrant/fisherfolk children (**Kolleru**).

137.s:
Consider the following statements about the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009:
1. It gives effect to Article 21A of the Constitution.
2. It covers children of the age of 6 to 14 years.
3. It came into force on 1 April 2010.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: All three are correct: the RTE Act gives effect to Article 21A, covers children aged 6-14 (elementary education, Classes 1-8, in a neighbourhood school) and came into force on 1 April 2010. Each other option leaves out a true statement.
137.tq: RTE: Art. 21A, 6-14 years, in force 1 April 2010.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **RTE Act 2009** gives effect to **Article 21A**, covers children **6-14**, and came into force on **1 April 2010**.
xa: APPSC: "6-14 years" and "enacted under Art. **21A**" are **both correct**.
**Section 3**: education in a **neighbourhood school** till **Classes 1-8**.
Full name: **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009**.

137.s:
Consider the following statements about child rights cases and portals:
1. Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India held that the RTE Act does not apply to minority schools.
2. The TrackChild Portal provides real-time digital tracking of Anganwadi service delivery, stunting, wasting and nutrition metrics for children aged 0–6 years.
3. The CARINGS portal is used for tracking missing, vulnerable and institutionalised children.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Pramati excluded aided and unaided minority schools from the RTE Act.
Statement 2: Incorrect: this is the Poshan Tracker app (WCD); TrackChild traces missing children.
Statement 3: Incorrect: CARINGS handles child adoption referrals and status tracking; TrackChild traces missing children.

137.s:
Consider the following statements about child education and rights bodies:
1. Samagra Shiksha (2018) merged only Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan, leaving out Teacher Education.
2. The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights consists of only a Chairperson and members nominated by the Supreme Court.
3. The Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016 is not among the Acts specifically monitored by the NCPCR.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education, all three.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the NCPCR has a Chairperson and six members, of whom at least two must be women; it is not made up of judicial nominees.
Statement 3: Correct: the stated mandate covers the JJ Act, 2015, the POCSO Act, 2012 and the RTE Act, 2009, not the Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016.

137.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Policy for Children:
1. Vocational employment is not one of the four priority areas of the National Policy for Children, 2013.
2. The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 operationalised the National Policy for Children, 2013.
3. The National Policy for Children, 2013 defines a child as a person below the age of 21 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the four priority areas are survival, health and nutrition; education and development; protection; and participation.
Statement 2: Correct: the 2016 Plan put the 2013 Policy into operation and follows the same four priority areas.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the Policy treats every person below 18, not 21, as a child; 21 is the marriage age for men.

137.s:
Consider the following statements about child protection laws and bodies:
1. The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) became a statutory body under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.
2. The child is defined as aged 6–14 years under POCSO, below 18 under child labour law and below 14 years under RTE.
3. Kushal Singh was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (2007).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x:
Statement 1: Correct: CARA became a statutory body under the JJ Act, 2015.
Statement 2: Incorrect: POCSO uses below 18, child labour law below 14, and RTE covers 6–14 years.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the NCPCR's first chairperson was Shanta Sinha, not Kushal Singh.

137.s:
Assertion (A): The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 was the first comprehensive child labour law.
Reason (R): The Children (Pledging of Labour) Act, 1933 was the first child labour law in India.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
137.x: Both are true: the 1986 Act was the first comprehensive child-labour law, and the Children (Pledging of Labour) Act, 1933, was the first child-labour law. An earlier law does not explain a later one, so R does not explain A.
137.tq: Ask whether an earlier law explains a later one.
n: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act was the first comprehensive Child Labour Law in 1986. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Children (Pledging of Labour) Act was the first Child Labour Law in India in 1933. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Child Labour Act was the first comprehensive Child Labour Law in the Children section in 1986. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xs: Both A and R are true, but **R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
The **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986** was the **first comprehensive** child labour law — true.
The **Children (Pledging of Labour) Act, 1933** was the **first child labour law** — true, but it does not explain the 1986 law.
xa: **Juvenile Justice Act**: first enacted **1986**.
**National Policy for Children**: first adopted **1974**; **ICDS**: **1975**.
**Tamil Nadu** pioneered the **Mid-Day Meal Scheme**.

137.s:
Consider the following statements about child protection portals:
1. The Khoya-Paya portal enables citizens to report missing or sighted children.
2. e-Baal Nidan is associated with adoption matching and referral services.
3. CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24×7 child helpline integrated with ERSS-112.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Khoya-Paya supports citizen reporting of missing or sighted children.
Statement 2: Incorrect: e-Baal Nidan is the NCPCR's online complaint portal for violations of child rights; CARINGS handles adoption.
Statement 3: Correct: CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24×7 child helpline now integrated with ERSS-112.

137.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two principal legal routes of adoption?
o: HAMA applies to specified religious communities, whereas the JJ route is open to all religions
HAMA is open to all religions, whereas the JJ route is restricted to Hindus
Both HAMA and the JJ route are restricted to Hindus
Neither route permits adoption by persons belonging to different religions
137.x: HAMA applies to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs, while the adoption route under the Juvenile Justice Act is open to all religions.
137.tq: Compare scope rather than confusing the two statutes because both concern adoption.
xs: **HAMA 1956** applies to **Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs**; the **JJ route** is **open to all religions** — option **(1)**.
So HAMA is not open to all, and the JJ route is not restricted to Hindus.
xa: **CARA** is statutory under the **JJ Act 2015**.
**Adoption Regulations 2022**: **2-month** reconsideration.
Debate: **arbitrariness** of the **JJ transfer system**.

137.s:
Consider the following statements about child education and welfare:
1. The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights lays down the minimum qualifications for appointment of teachers under the RTE framework.
2. Under the RTE Act, the Centre does not bear sole financial responsibility for implementing the Act.
3. As per the provisional figures of Census 2011, the child sex ratio (0-6 years) of India was 1,020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the minimum teacher qualifications are laid down by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE).
Statement 2: Correct: funds for the RTE Act are shared by the Centre and the States.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the child sex ratio in Census 2011 was 914; 1,020 is the overall sex ratio in NFHS-5.

137.s: Which of the following aspects has been included in the list of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution?
o: Reservation for SCs and STs in promotions
Free and compulsory education to children up to the age of 14 years
Hoisting national flag at one's residence
137.x: The right to free and compulsory education for children up to the age of 14 was elevated to a Fundamental Right through the 86th Constitutional Amendment, inserting Article 21A. The other listed items are either statutory provisions or matters covered under other parts of the Constitution.

137.s: Which Article of the Constitution of India says, "No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment"? Indian Polity: Constitutional Framework PMF IAS IP – 18
137.x: Article 24 of the Constitution of India prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any other hazardous occupations. It is a Fundamental Right under Part III of the Constitution and aims to protect children from exploitation and hazardous working conditions. Article 45 relates to early childhood care and education; Article 330 deals with the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha; and Article 368 lays down the procedure for amending the Constitution.

137.s: Right to Education Act came into force from:
137.x: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act came into effect on 1 April 2010.

137.s: When was the Right to Education added through the amendment in the Constitution of India?

The online portal _________, developed by the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) in 2015 for redressal of grievances against violation of child rights, was updated in September 2022.
Which of the following is not a priority area of National Policy on Education?
137.x: Compulsory nutrition education for all is not listed as a stated priority area of the National Policy on Education, unlike universal elementary education, adult literacy, and women's educational equality.

137.s: Which of the following is not a priority area of National Policy on Education?
o: A. Compulsory nutrition education to all
